# Decisions and history (archive)

Not loaded automatically. This is the full record behind the rules in
`CLAUDE.md`, `DESIGN.md` and `STANDARD.md`: why each rule exists, what was
reported, what was measured. Search it before changing an area
(`grep -n "<area>" docs/DECISIONS.md`). New history is added here, one entry
per change; the rule itself goes in exactly one loaded file.

Part 1 is `CLAUDE.md` and part 2 is `STANDARD.md` §24 (Project Memory), both
verbatim as they stood on 2026-09-26. `DESIGN.md` as it stood is in
`docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md`.

# Part 1. CLAUDE.md as of 2026-09-26

# ADspace Digital Portal — working rules

@DESIGN.md
@STANDARD.md

Static site, vanilla JS, no build step, served by GitHub Pages at
digital.adspace.me (CNAME in the repo). Pages: `admin/` (console),
`creators/` (client-facing creator selection), `review/` (client-facing
content review). Supabase behind `js/api.js`; schema in
`supabase/schema.sql` (re-runnable; the user runs it by hand in the SQL
editor, and must be told when). A change confined to one function or one
column ships instead as a dated file in `supabase/migrations/`, narrowly
scoped and safe to run twice, so a live database is not put through fifteen
unrelated data migrations to replace one function body.

The design system, the components, the laws and the copy rules are in
`DESIGN.md`. The general engineering and design standard, the working method
and the completion gate are in `STANDARD.md`, whose Project Memory records the
three places this portal deliberately departs from it (the spacing scale, the
14px console body, and the 1280/390 viewport matrix). Both are imported above. Read all
three before any change; where they disagree, `STANDARD.md` §2 settles it and
this portal's documented behaviour wins.

## 1. Verified code engine

### Locked features (merged to `main`, PRs #3 to #52)

| Area | Locked behaviour |
|---|---|
| Theme (`css/portal.css`, `js/admin.js`) | Light is the default everywhere and never taken from `prefers-color-scheme`. Dark is the console's alone, chosen from a toggle in the sidebar foot above Sign out, kept in `localStorage` as `adspace-theme`, applied by a head script before first paint, and hung off `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. `/client/`, `/creators/` and `/review/` never carry the attribute, so a client never decides on a proposal in a register nobody chose. |
| Screen typeface | System stack for everything except the display sizes, which take Slate Regular through `--font-head` (`/css/SlateRg.woff2`, 38KB, `font-display: swap`; the TTF stays for pdf-lib and as the fallback). Optima is the letterhead wordmark and stays out of the portal. |
| The wordmark keeps its proportions (`css/portal.css` `.brand-logo`, `index.html`, `404.html`, 2026-09-21) | **`height` plus `width: auto` plus the global `img { max-width: 100% }` is a squash waiting for a narrow box.** The width is clamped to what is left and the height is not, so the mark is compressed horizontally and the wordmark stops being the wordmark — reported by the user on 2026-09-21. Measured in the 244px console rail, where the box settles at 195px: every stand-in past **8.13:1 drew at 8.13:1**, ratio 10 and ratio 14 landing on the same squashed figure, and the wider the asset the worse it got; the top bar has room at 1280 and would fail the same way in a narrower one. The fix cannot depend on the asset's intrinsic ratio — `brandLogo` is served from the CDN, which the sandbox's network policy blocks, and a new file can be uploaded any day — so it is **`object-fit: contain` with `object-position: left center`**: the ink fits whatever box the layout gives it with the ratio true and sits on the rail's own margin instead of centred in the leftover width. The box still measures its stated height, so nothing under it moves; what gives is the drawn height of a mark too wide for the rail. The two root pages take the same two declarations on `.doorbar img`. Measured with stand-ins of stated ratios (6, 8, 10, 12, 14) before and after, because the mechanism does not depend on knowing the real one. |
| The sign-in page holds still (`js/chrome.js`, `css/portal.css`, `admin/index.html`, 2026-09-26) | **Reported by the user: the header moved on load, and on a phone the mark was missing.** Measured before the fix: the mark lands from the CDN after the first paint and an image with no file has no width, so the page label jumped **208px** right when it arrived; the footer was added at `DOMContentLoaded`, so the sign-in card, centred between the bar and the floor, moved **26px** up when the floor rose; and the page was grey until the session was read, then white. Now: **the mark's proportions are kept from the last visit** (`adspace-logo-ratio` in `localStorage`, written on load) and the box is drawn at that size from the first paint (`aspect-ratio: auto R`, replaced by the file's own ratio once it loads); **on a first visit the brand is held back** (`.brand.is-waiting`, `visibility: hidden`) until the mark loads or fails, at most 2.5s, so it arrives once, in place. `ADspaceChrome.mark()` (the console rail) reserves the same way. **The footer is drawn with the header** and sits last on the screen from the first paint (`.portalfoot { order: 1 }` in the body's flex column), then is moved to the end of the body once the page is parsed, so the keyboard and a screen reader reach it last; `body:has(> .console:not([hidden])) > .portalfoot` hides it while the footer still precedes the console. **The first paint knows whether a session is kept** (`data-boot` from the head script, off an `sb-*-auth-token` key; `js/admin.js` `gate()` removes it, and so does a 4s timeout): signed out is white from the start, signed in draws no sign-in bar or footer for a frame over the console about to open. **The phone mark**: `.topbar .brand-logo` is `flex: 0 0 auto; max-width: 60vw`, because Safari resolves the global `img { max-width: 100% }` against a `.brand` that is sized by its own content and, on a phone where the label beside the mark is hidden, drew the mark 0px wide; a `vw` cap needs no container. Verified in Chromium by measuring the bar every frame through load at 1280 and 390, first visit and second; **Safari itself cannot be run in the sandbox**, so the phone mark is fixed on the mechanism and is the user's to confirm. **The bar and the foot run to the screen's edges on every page** (`.topbar-inner, .portalfoot-in { max-width: none }`; the user, 2026-09-26: the header "still moves and center-aligned … when the browser gets larger"): the sign-in page was the last to keep the centred 1240px box, so its mark slid across as the window widened; it now sits at x=24 at every width, where the rail's mark sits once the console opens. |
| The rail's activity glyphs (`js/crm.js` `SECTION_ICON` / `logIcon`, 2026-09-21) | **A section with no glyph draws the bare dot, which reads as a fault beside rows that have one.** `SECTION_ICON` was missing `register` (Documents) and `ops` (My Work), and `logIcon` tested `/^doc\./` where every tag this portal writes is `document.*` or `register.*` — so a letter issued against a client drew a hollow circle in Recent activity. Found by **reading** the walk screenshot the first time the Activity pane was seeded with rows: the fault had been on the screen since the block shipped, and no screenshot anywhere had ever contained a row to show it. That seed is now in the walk (`tests/uxaudit.js`, three rows on the Laman Citra record, names long enough to exercise the `By` column and a detail long enough to wrap), because a pane that walks empty is a pane whose one row shape nobody has measured. |
| No profile-image placeholders (`js/crm.js`, `js/campaigns.js`, `js/ops.js`, `css/portal.css`, 2026-09-21) | **A mark holds artwork or it is not a mark.** Two monogram discs survived the creators list's removal because neither sat on a list of creators: `.log-avatar`, a 28px disc of one initial beside the actor on every row of the client's and the campaign's Activity panes, and `.bcard-face`, a 20px initials disc beside the owner on every board card with a **dashed empty one** where there was no owner. Both stand in for a profile picture this portal holds none of and is not going to — no avatar exists anywhere in the data model — so each drew the same grey circle down every row, and where the letter did vary it said nothing the full name beside it had not already said. A dashed empty circle standing for an unassigned task is a placeholder for a placeholder. The log row is `.log-who` > `.log-person` and the board card's foot is the owner's name; `actorInitial()` is gone from both files. **What stays and why**: `.rec-mark` holds the client's own `logo_url` and falls back to initials only while we wait for one, and `.mk-avatar` carries that logo into a platform's own UI on the review mockups — both hold real artwork. Every other circle in the stylesheet was checked in the same pass and is a real logo (`.bigcard-logo`, `.logopreview`), a glyph (`.ovlog-ico`), a control (`.iconbtn` and its kin) or a platform mockup's own furniture. The global Activity record (`js/admin.js`) already drew its actor as plain text. |
| Header and footer (`js/chrome.js`) | One chrome on every page: mark from `brandLogo`, kicker from `data-kicker`, actions from `data-actions` (`lang`, `qr`); "Digital Portal" and "Logged in as {email}" in the console; outlined Sign out with icon. Footer left `© {year} ADSPACE PLT. All Rights Reserved.`, right `Terms of Service` → https://adspacestudios.com/legal/policies; footer on the floor on short pages. |
| Full-page states | One `.cover` component for no link, bad link, access code, closed, confirmed, nothing to review, access denied; same words on `creators/` and `review/`. |
| Content Review (`review/`, `js/review.js`, `js/mockups.js`) | Post mockups per platform (Instagram feed 4:5 1080×1350, Reels and Stories 9:16 at cover ratio, TikTok, Facebook feed and carousel, rednote); Facebook carousel: 2 tiles side by side, 4 as 2×2, 5 as 2 above 3 with `+N` greyed on the fifth; handle shown on the mockup, not the client name; client logo fills the circle with no border or shadow; placeholder avatar is an illuminance gradient, never grey or rainbow; Approve needs a name and Approved reads outlined with Request changes hidden; Copywriting label, copy text control at the top; the Instagram send glyph is the one concave dart Instagram draws, not Feather's `send` (a quadrilateral plus a separate crease from the same apex: at 22px with a round cap the two strokes pile up at that corner and the mark reads as a smudge), because a mockup is only a preview while every mark in it is the one the client's audience sees; **the caption block is spaced the way the app spaces it**: Save hangs off the far right of the action row (`.mk-act-save`, `margin-left: auto`) and never sits against Share, the `more` toggle rides the end of the truncated line over a short fade (`.mk-clampwrap.is-clamped`, both ends of the width stated so it animates) rather than taking a row of its own, and a blank line between paragraphs is collapsed **while the caption is clamped** (`.mk-clamp br + br`), because `<br><br>` spent one of the two preview lines on nothing and printed the ellipsis on an empty row; likes, caption and comments are one block of text, so the three gaps that separate them are the same 4px; no Save as PDF; og:title `{client name} Content Review Portal by ADspace` on `review/` only. |
| Console: Content Review | Content sets folded, one open at a time; Publish / Unpublish (warn); resend for approval with a note; Google Drive import with a progress bar; S3 upload by signed PUT; only active clients listed. **Deleting a content set is `can_remove`, and the icon is drawn behind it** (`body.no-remove #deleteSet`): it takes the set's posts and their approval records with it and there is no restore, so it is the same authority as a client, a letter, a contact or a short link, and it was the one hard delete in the console whose control was drawn for everybody. A Marketing group without the permission was offered a trash icon that could not work. **A delete that removes nothing is not a success**: `db.from('batches').delete()` and `db.from('posts').delete()` both reported one. PostgREST answers a refused delete with 204 and **no error at all** — the row simply stays — so the set panel closed, nothing was said, and the set was still in the list underneath; the post delete was worse and threw its answer away entirely. Both take `.select('id')` now and name the refusal (`Not deleted. The database refused the request.`) rather than repainting a list that has not changed. `tests/setdel.js` drives all three states and `tests/stub2.js` can refuse a delete the way RLS does (`window.__refuseDelete = { batches: true }`), because a stand-in that cannot say no is one that cannot test a refusal. |
| Console: Clients (`js/crm.js`) | **One set of handles per client, not two.** The Brand profile held `social_*` and Content Review's client settings held `handle_*`, over the same row, so a handle corrected on the record left the one printed on the client's own mockup untouched. Brand now edits the `handle_*` columns the review page reads and the mockups print, and carries the **client logo** (`logo_url`) with the same disc preview, which is also the record's mark. `social_*` is backfilled by `handle_of()` — a bare handle as typed, a pasted profile URL's last segment, and **nothing at all where that segment is a route** (`instagram.com/p/DXyz` would otherwise print `DXyz` on a client's post) — and is never written again. The links row derives each address from the handle per platform (`profileUrl()`), because `https://` + `@starliving` is nothing. **Delete client** is in the record's ⋯, behind `can_remove` (`body.no-remove #crmClientMenuWrap`), a sheet that counts what goes from the record already loaded and takes the client's name typed back, plus the delete code where `delete_code_set()` says one exists; `delete_client` re-checks `allowed('remove')` when the button is pressed. Paused and Past remain how a client leaves the working list; this is for the lead keyed in twice. Lead intake (Brand name, the trading name; the registered company name is Billing's; Source, Contact person, phone, email, Enquiry; Owner, Industry, Market); record in sale order; contacts as a table; Billing details fold with ring summary and billing contact from Contacts; Brand profile fold; Calls and visits with next actions and Undo; a stage clock (`stage_since`, `stage_log`, stamped by the `clients_stage_clock` trigger) showing time in the current stage under the chip on the list and the whole journey as one line on the record, with `client.stage` as its own activity tag; ageing off `STALE_H` (Lead 48 hours, Proposal sent 21 days, calendar days, Contacted unset) marking an over-run stage "2 days · Overdue" in warn and counting them in the group head; Services lines (qty × rate × months from a start date, Enquired / To quote / Confirmed, prefilled not fixed); Documents (the Letter of Offer); Engagements only once Active; stage select on the head with the Active gate. **Urgency to commence** (`clients.commence`: 1 to 3 months / 3 to 6 months / 6 months or more, blank until asked) on the intake form and the record, because the stage clock measures how long we have taken and not how long the client will wait. **The enquiry is edited like every other fact about the client**: it used to sit in the intake-only block with the contact fields, so it could be typed once at the door and never again; the contact fields stay at intake, because after that a person is a row in Contacts. **On a phone the row is a two column table**, not a card with the chip pushed right: name over meta on the left, the state chip over the age in a **fixed 120px track** on the right (measured against its worst case, "18 months · Overdue" at 119px), both top aligned. The meta line carries the deal value where there is one and omits what is not known, never a bare currency sign standing in for a figure. **Three bands, in the order somebody works them**: **Leads** first (speed to first contact is the number that moves conversion, and a lead under a hundred and eighty clients is a lead nobody rings), **Clients** (active *and* paused — a paused client is still a client and reads wrong filed under an ending, so the working book of business is one thing to scan), and **Past clients** (ended engagements, **shut by default** and remembered, because nobody opens this page to read one; they keep their place and their count rather than disappearing, since they are still clients, still hold their number, and may renew). A band is a `<button>` carrying its count, so it clears the control floor (`--ctl-h-sm`) like every other control — `.svc-cat`'s own padding left it at 42px and `uxaudit`'s `target` rule is what said so. **A filter opens every band**, because somebody who searched for a name wants the row wherever it is and a shut band would hide the one match and say nothing. Each band draws its first thirty with `Show N more` under it. **The Client ID is on the row**, under the name, in the token face: a seventh column would cost the name its width on every row for a number only read with an invoice in hand, and the phone template has nowhere to put it; it is searched alongside the two names. The ID itself is unchanged — manual, `^[A-Z0-9]{2,12}$`, unique, and load bearing, because the Letter of Offer serial is `AQL/{client_code}/{YYMM}{SEQ}`. **The list is a card per stage**, drawn by `js/group.js` like every other directory (`ADspaceGroup.section`: `.crm-group` > `.crm-group-head` + `.crm-group-body` > `.crm-table.softpanel.crm-register`): Leads, Clients and Past clients each under its own 15px heading carrying the count and the overdue mark, each table with its own header row, the stage's name the fold (`.crm-group-fold`), which opens and shuts the card in place. It was one surface with the stages as uppercase `.svc-cat.crm-band` divider rows for a week; the user sent that back on 2026-09-22 (the eyebrow face and its spacing read as wrong) and asked for the cards the rate card uses for Services and Add-ons, so the Register is drawn the same way (a card per family, newest first, a sort in the bar). Columns are Client, Stage, Industry, Person in charge, **Last activity** (no Value column and no value on a heading, 2026-09-26: what a client is worth is read on the record's Services; a card's rows run **newest Client ID first**, digits compared as numbers, unnumbered records after them newest first) (`loadLastSeen()`: the newest of a logged call or visit, the stage moving (`stage_since`, `Added` while it has never moved) and a document issued (a Letter of Offer or a Documents row), the date over a small mute word saying which, the user's choice of 2026-09-26; each read is one the record already makes, a refused one is left out rather than failing the column, and a date ahead of now is a plan and never counts) and the chevron in the column the header leaves empty. **The row is one `<button>`** with nothing nested in it, so the whole of it opens the workspace from a pointer and from the keyboard alike. Every state is a screen somebody lands on and every one is driven by `tests/register.js`: populated, loading, empty, filtered empty and refused, at 1280 and 390. **The empty states are `ADspaceState.emptyLine`**, not a private copy of the same markup. **A filter repaints only when the filter changed**: `input` and `change` both fire for one keystroke and the second arrives on **blur**, so pressing Clear the filters blurred the search box, repainted the list, and detached the button between mousedown and click — the one way out of a filtered empty list did nothing at all when it was clicked with a mouse, and a test that dispatched the event instead of clicking it could not see that. |
| Console: Clients, the record's identity and Overview (`js/crm.js` `paintIdentity` / `paintSummary`) | **The identity is two parts, and they centre on each other.** Left: the mark, then `.rec-who` (the name with its stage select on one line, the meta line under them). Right: `.rec-ctl`, one ⋯ holding **Edit** and **Delete client** (the delete item alone carries `data-need="clients:manage"`; the ⋯ itself draws for everybody). The campaign head has the same shape with **Edit details** in its ⋯. Edit used to sit beside the stage on every record, and on a phone it and the ⋯ wrapped to a line of their own under the name with the meta below them, which is the wrong reading order and the loosest part of the card spent on its rarest act; and on a desktop the controls sat on the name line, above the card's centre on every record with a meta line. `.rec-id` is `auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto` with `align-items: center`, so a long name wraps under itself and the state follows it, and the ⋯ stays on the middle of the card at every width. **On a phone the two parts are two rows** (`.is-narrow .rec-id`: `"mark . ctl" / "who who who"`): the 38px mark at the top left, the state chip and the ⋯ at the top right, then who this is under them full width on the card's own margin. Beside the mark the name had 130px, a campaign's chip wrapped under it, and the campaign's purpose line, drawn outside the grid, sat on a different margin from the name and the meta. The campaign's `.camp-purpose` is the second of three lines inside `.rec-who` (name, purpose, client · person in charge) and its chip lives in `.rec-ctl` beside the ⋯ at every width. `tests/six.js` measures the ⋯ against the card's centre at 1280, and at 390 that the mark and the ⋯ share the top row and who this is sits under them on the mark's margin; both widths assert Edit is in the menu. **The campaign's state chip is centred on the ⋯ beside it** (`.rec-ctl .chip { align-self: center }`): the shared `.chip` rule pins a chip to the top of its flex row, so the state sat 11px above the control's centre and read as squeezed in beside the dots rather than on the same line; `tests/six.js` measures the two centres at 1280 and 390. **The rate card row is the same height with or without its ⋯** (`.is-narrow .cat-row > .team-act` takes the roster's negative block margin): the ⋯ draws for an admin only, and its 44px target had made the same row 97px on an admin's phone and 68px on everybody else's. **The client's stage select is in `.rec-ctl` beside the ⋯**, the shape the campaign head already had: on the name line it stood mid line on a phone with nothing to its right. **Below 1100 the rail splits around the panes**: `.rec:not(.cportal) > .rec-rail` is `display: contents` and its blocks take `order`, so Account status, Next action, the billing gate and Profile come before the tab strip and the three `.rail-after` blocks (Key dates, Details, Recent activity) follow the pane; one rail above the tabs had put the record's own content a screen and a half down on a phone. The client portal is excluded, because its contact rows key on the rail's own width class and a rail that is not a box has none. `tests/six.js` asserts the select's centre against the ⋯ at both widths and the block order at 390. **Key dates draws no rule under nothing** (`.raildates:empty + .rail-date-edit`): every date row is omitted when the record does not hold it, so a client with none showed a heading, a gap and a hairline over an empty list. Its Save is an outlined `.btn-sm` centred on the field (`align-items: center`), not a bare word bottom-aligned against a box of another height. **The record opens on an identity area, not a title strip.** `.rec-id` carries a 46px mark — the client's own `logo_url` where we hold one, their initials where we do not (`initialsOf()`: two characters of a Chinese name, the first letters of the first two **letter-initial** words otherwise, so Dale & Cecil is DC and not "D&") — the name, the stage select, Edit, and a meta line naming the main contact's preferred language and the person in charge, each omitted when it is not known. The disc stays light in both themes for the reason the review mockups do: a client's logo is their artwork and is not ours to invert. **The Overview is an operational record**: one `.ovcard` surface of flat titled sections divided by hairlines — Contact details, Services, Letters, Calls and visits — each a heading, the one control that opens its pane (`Edit` with the pen on Contact details, `Manage services ›`, `View all ›`), and concise real rows (`.ovfacts` as label beside value in a 150px track, 104px when narrow, never eyebrow-over-value two across; `.ovtable` with stated tracks; `.ovlog` with a glyph per kind of call). Built **only from what the record has already loaded** (contacts, service lines, documents, touches): no second read, no stored number, no invented metric, no new field, RPC, permission or workflow. Enquired service lines are not shown, for the reason the letter leaves them out. A section with nothing says so in one line rather than disappearing, because "None issued." is itself an answer. **The rail is one block per question** (`.railblock`, each with a `.railtitle` at the pane's own 15px section size, not an eyebrow): **Account status** (the stage chip and the stage clock, `12 days in this stage`, with `· Overdue` in warn where `isStale()` says so; Active for left Key dates when this arrived, so the clock is stated once), Next action, the **billing gate** (`.railgate`: a red `--err` block, drawn only while a billing field is missing on a record not yet Active, a button that opens Billing where `maySeeBilling()`, plain otherwise; it was an amber `.notice` reading "Not active." on every lead, which is a caution's colour on a refusal), Profile (the completion bar), Key dates, Details, Recent activity. Key dates and Recent activity rows carry a neutral 16px glyph (`RICON` / `ico()` in `js/crm.js`: calendar, phone, pin, person, file, tag, image, speaker, link), and the Overview's calls do too, in a 30px `--sunk` disc. **Next action prefers the one a person wrote** (`client_touches.next_action` / `next_at`, overdue in warn) over the step `nextStep()` derives, because a person decided it and a derivation did not. **Record completion is a bar with the missing list under it**, never a bare figure, counted over billing, brand, contacts and services. **Key dates omit a row whose date is not there** (Client since from `created_at`, Last contact and Next follow up from touches). **Recent activity is the last three `activity_log` rows**, read once when the record opens and kept in `state.log`, so the Activity pane no longer re-reads. **A block leaves entirely when its data does not exist**, so the rule under the last one is a class `paintRail` sets: `:last-child` counts a hidden sibling. Person in charge is on the identity line and Added is in Key dates, so neither is repeated in Details. **`.rec` states `grid-template-rows: auto 1fr`**: the rail spans both rows, so with `auto auto` a rail taller than tabs plus pane had its extra shared between them and a lead opened with sixty pixels of nothing between its tab strip and its first section. |
| The client record's Timeline (`js/crm.js` `railDates` / `journeyOf`, 2026-09-21) | **Every date and every duration in one block, and the durations are the point.** Asked for by the user on 2026-09-21: the record stated its durations in three places and none of them answered the question the team actually has. `Leads 10 days · Active today` sat as a mute line under Details, `Active · Since today` in the rail's Account status, and Key dates held only `Client since` — so "how long does a lead wait to be contacted" could not be read anywhere. **Key dates is Timeline**, because a block holding `9 days` is not a block of dates: the stage journey is a row per stage above a rule (the stage, when it began, how long it ran) and the dates the record holds are the rows below it. **Each stage row is one of the turnarounds a report will average later** — time in Lead is speed to first contact, time in Contacted is contact to proposal, time in Proposal sent is how long it took to close, time in Active is how long this client has been engaged — and **nothing new is stored for any of it**: `stage_log` has been stamped by the `clients_stage_clock` trigger since it shipped, so the averages across every client need no field, no migration and no backfill. **The stage that is running carries the weight and the overdue mark** (`.tl-row.is-now`, `isStale()`), which is why **the Account status block is gone**: the stage select in the head says where the record stands and this says for how long, and a rail block repeating the head's own control was the same fact twice. That supersedes the 2026-09-21 decision that "the rail opens on Account status (stage chip plus stage clock)". **Client since is edited where it sits** (`ADspaceAsk.rename` with `type: 'date'` and `value`, `#crmSinceVal` + `#crmSinceEdit`): the value on the row becomes the picker and the pen beside it becomes the tick, so the separate labelled field and Save button under the list are gone — the shape `js/ask.js` already gave every value already on the screen, extended once so a date can seed its field with `2026-06-01` while the row reads `12 Aug 2026`. The save takes `.select('id')` and names a refusal, like every other write a policy can refuse. **The row is two tracks and not three**: a name, a date and a duration are all `nowrap`, and three of them measured at exactly 365px in a 365px rail — no slack at all, so the first longer stage name pushed the page sideways, which `uxaudit`'s `overflow` rule caught on the first run. The duration ends the row on its own margin and the date rides mute beside the name. The pen is `--ctl-h` with the rate card's negative block margin, because the audit's control floor is 38px and `--ctl-h-sm` is for `.btn-sm` and its kin. **Every stage date is editable too** (2026-09-25, the user: a client keyed in today who has been a client since April read "Lead, today"): each stage row carries its own pen beside its duration, the stage moves still fill the dates in, **Client since is the first stage's start** so moving one moves the other, a stage may not begin before the one before it and no date is in the future, and one save writes `stage_log`, `stage_since` (the last entry) and `created_at` together. Sign-ups stay closed on the project, which is what stops the page minting accounts; `signInWithOtp` carries `shouldCreateUser: false` and `portal-login` is what puts the account there first. **One address can hold access at several clients** (`portal_clients()` returns every one), so a group of companies is one login with a company select on the page. The page reads and writes only through `get_portal`, `portal_request` and `portal_withdraw` (security definer, keyed on the signed-in email); a client account never touches a table. Sections in order: Overview (registered name, registration no., billing address, market, account manager, status chip; contacts read-only; one action Request change), Services (confirmed and quoted lines with chips and totals; enquired lines never shown; Upgrade / Downgrade / Cancel in the ⋯ of a confirmed line), Requests (appears once one exists; Withdraw while Requested, with Undo), Letters (Download redraws the snapshot), Engagements (Content Review and each campaign opened by their own token links; hidden when there is nothing), Payment (only once `ADSPACE_ORG.bank` is set), **Portal access** (Person · Sign-in email: the client's own people who hold a sign-in, named for that rather than "Account", which read as the viewer's own settings). English and Chinese. Covers: Client sign-in / Check your email / Access denied / Unable to load. |

### Non-negotiable validation before "done"

**The behavioural suites are in `adspaceplt/digital-form-tests`, a private
repository.** This one is public, and the harness, the database schema and
these working notes were all reachable at digital.adspace.me and readable on
github.com; the suites were taken out on the user's instruction on 2026-09-20.
`_config.yml` stops Pages publishing the rest.

**They are cloned beside the portal and linked in**, which is the first thing
to do in a new session, before changing behaviour:

```
git clone https://github.com/adspaceplt/digital-form-tests /home/user/digital-form-tests
ln -sfn /home/user/digital-form-tests /home/user/digital-form/tests
```

The symlink is what lets every suite go on taking `tests` as its argument and
reading `tests/stub2.js` beside itself; `.gitignore` holds both `tests` and
`tests/`, because a symlink is not a directory and the trailing slash alone
does not match it. **A repair to a suite is committed and pushed to that
repository in the same batch as the change it covers**, or it is lost with the
container.

**Every suite the sweep below names now exists** (2026-09-21). `docs.js`,
`cmdbar.js`, `six.js` and `sch.js` were the last four that had been written
after `02de7c9` and never reached a commit anywhere; they are written again
and pass. `docs.js` needed the **Documents Register half of `tests/stub2.js`**,
which did not exist at all — `documents`, a seeded `doc_types`, the seven
functions, and the read policy in `builder()` so an HR row never arrives where
`register.hr` is not held. It also needs `npm i --prefix tests/pdfx`, and
prints `docs: SKIP` loudly where that has not been run.

**It was lost with the container, for three days, and that is why this section
reads the way it does.** Between 2026-09-20 and the move, the instruction here
was `git checkout 02de7c9 -- tests`, and every session dutifully restored,
repaired, ran and then deleted the folder — so the same repair was paid for
again each session and never survived one. By the time it was measured, that
restore point was eight pull requests behind the product: **eight suites
passed, thirteen crashed, and twelve had been written after `02de7c9` and
never reached a commit anywhere**, `ops.js` and `work.js` among them. Those
twelve are gone and are being written again; `STATUS.md` in that repository is
the live register of which suite is in which state, and is what to read before
claiming the gate ran.

Everything below still applies. What changed is where the suites live, not
whether they are run: a portal this size cannot be checked by reading it.

1. `node --check` on every changed `js/*.js`.
2. Local server: `setsid nohup npx --yes http-server -p 8899 -s . >/dev/null 2>&1 &` from the repo root (it dies between turns; restart on `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`).
3. The full behavioural sweep, every suite green. **Read the exit code, never a count of `FAIL` lines**: a suite that throws — a locator that times out because the control it names has been removed, a native time field filled with `2pm` — prints no `FAIL` line at all, so `grep -c '^FAIL'` reports zero and the sweep reads a crash as a pass. That is how `tests/crm.js` sat broken on `main`, and how `tests/prod.js` sat dead from its bulk-logistics section onward.
   `for s in run camp client cprod bar newbadge prod qr regress backup keyin state race chrome crm sgd team portal creator canvas register geom letter links sets setdel six sch undo levels trail docs work cmdbar qc perfui keys slide perms cprofile perfguard pwa reports adsreport signin phone camptime datefloor passkey; do out=$(node tests/$s.js tests 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "$s: CRASHED rc=$rc"; else echo "$s: $(echo "$out" | tail -1)"; fi; done`
3a. **The wider matrix and the keyboard: `node tests/matrix.js tests` → `matrix: ok`.** A representative screen from every route at **320, 375, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440**, and again at 1280 and 1440 under **200% browser zoom** — the CSS viewport halved, not the `zoom` property, because Ctrl + is what a reader presses and it fires the media queries. It runs `uxaudit`'s own `inPage()` checks, read out of that file rather than copied, so a rule added there is a rule the matrix enforces, and drives the keyboard through every control that opens a dialog.
3b. **For any change to the operations system: `node tests/ops.js tests` → `ops: ok`.** It runs the dated migration against a throwaway Postgres 16, twice, with the real `allowed()` and `level_rank()` cut out of `supabase/schema.sql` rather than restated, and drives the permission gates, the stage machine, the commitment history, assignment, work sessions, revisions, the client's decision, completion, recurring generation and the append-only audit trail. It also compares each canonical schema section with its own migration byte for byte, cutting phase 1 at phase 2's banner: a cut with no end marker takes everything appended to the file afterwards. **The page is `node tests/work.js tests` → `work: ok`**, which drives the queue, the workspace, the stage machine and its refusals, the timer and the permission classes against `tests/stub2.js`.
3b2. **For any change to performance reviews: `node tests/perf.js tests` → `perf: ok`** (real Postgres, the migration twice, the mirror compared) **and `node tests/perfui.js tests` → `perfui: ok`** (both pages against `tests/stub2.js`, whose `perfRpc` mirrors every function and refusal, with a fixture code of its own that is never the live one).
3c. **For any change to `supabase/schema.sql`, including a seed or a function: `node tests/sql.js tests` → `sql: ok`.** It starts a throwaway Postgres 16 cluster and runs the real thing: the stage clock, the team sweep and repair, the overlap guard, the rate card seed, the whole creator delivery path, the client's recorded decision, the creator rating and the handle reader. Every other suite drives a browser against `stub2.js`, so PL/pgSQL is the one part of the portal nothing else checks. It builds its own cut-down tables, so a column added to the schema has to be added to that fixture too. It prints `SKIP` loudly where Postgres is missing rather than passing quietly.
4. `node tests/uxaudit.js tests` → must print `uxaudit: ok`. **Read that line, never the exit code**: the walk exits 0 on `uxaudit: PROBLEM (18 fail)` as well, and on 2026-09-22 a run with eighteen failures was read as green from its exit code and a PR opened on it. It walks every page and state at 1280 and at 390 with a coarse pointer, and the console again in dark at both widths, and fails on: sideways overflow, a cell alone on its row, uneven card padding, a header cell off its column (`cols`), the same cell starting at different x on different rows (`column`), a last column that ends short of the row's right edge on a phone (`edge`), uneven gaps between the blocks of a section (`stack`), text under 11px (`type`), a value that wraps or clips, buttons in one row at different heights (or widths on a phone), a control under 38px (44px touch; `.btn-sm`, `.input-sm`, `.select-sm` may be 32px on desktop), a field or icon-only button without a name, more than two filled actions in a view, text under 4.5:1, a control border under 3:1, a control that takes focus without a ring, and a row whose way out is drawn before its action (`order`). The review page's post mockups (`.card-stage`) are outside the audit. **A new route or pane is added to the walk in the same push that builds it**, and to `tests/matrix.js`'s route list: a screen nobody walks is a screen whose alignment, contrast and touch targets nobody measured, and the walk is the only thing that compares two pages against each other.
5. Screenshots at 1280 and 390 of every screen the change touches, in both themes when the change is visual (`SHOTS=1 node tests/uxaudit.js tests` for the whole walk into `tests/walk/`). Each one is opened and read against the phone checklist in `DESIGN.md`, not just taken.
6. For any PDF change: `node tests/pdfreal.js tests` and `node tests/pdfcases.js tests` → `pdfcases: ok`, which draws the letter against the extremes one fixture never reaches and asserts what only geometry can say — the four AcroForm fields exist as widgets with valid rectangles, the execution block is all on one page, and nothing drawn crosses the margins, read back from glyph positions with pdf.js because a clipped string decodes perfectly as text. `node tests/pdfshot.js tests <file.pdf>` rasterises a letter. Both need `npm i pdfjs-dist@3.11.174 --prefix tests/pdfx` and the local server.
7. Version stamp: every stylesheet and script tag carries `?v=YYYYMMDD` (`20260920a`, `b`… for further pushes the same day). Bump on every push that changes CSS or JS with one `sed` over every HTML file that carries one.
8. The deploy is confirmed from the GitHub Pages workflow run for the merge commit (`pages build and deployment`, conclusion success). `curl` to digital.adspace.me returns 403 from the sandbox and proves nothing.

## 4. Workflow and constraints

### Git and delivery
- Branch `cl/exciting-mayer-fvg0dc`; one PR per batch, squash-merged to `main` by Claude; after a merge the branch is reset onto `origin/main` (`git checkout -B … origin/main`, force-with-lease push). Never stack on merged history.
- Commit message: a one-line title in plain English about what the person gains, a body in the same register, then the two trailers from the session reminder. PR body: What changed, Test plan (ticked), the two footer lines. No model identifiers in any repo artifact.
- The user is in "proceed and merge" mode: build, test, push, open the PR, merge, confirm the Pages build, then report. Ask only when readings differ materially; never re-explain settled decisions.
- When a schema change ships, the report says "re-run `supabase/schema.sql`" in the user-side list. Edge functions (`sign-upload`, `invite-member`, Verify JWT off) are deployed by the user with the Supabase CLI.
- Never ask for a URL, key or asset the repo or config already holds (`brandLogo`, favicon, fonts in `css/`). Check `js/config.js` and `css/` first.

### Folder and file rules
- **`index.html` is the portal's front door and is now ours**: a cover carrying the mark and `Digital Portal` and nothing else, built from `css/portal.css` so it shares the portal's tokens, and needing no script. **White to the browser's edge** (2026-09-24, the user: "white background, together with the browser header"): `background: var(--card)`, `<meta name="theme-color" content="#ffffff">` and `color-scheme: light`, because a cover with no cards on it has nothing to lift off an off-white ground; the name is **15px, 500, in `--ink-soft`**, not the 22 to 30px display face ("smaller words, to be more minimalist and modern"), so the mark leads. No sign in and no menu of the rooms inside: every door into this portal is a link somebody was sent (the console behind Supabase Auth, the client pages behind their own tokens), so a list of them would be an index of what exists and a set of dead ends for anybody without a link. The user asked for it on 2026-09-20; the rule below still holds for every other root file.
- **`404.html` is the portal's too, from 2026-09-21**, at the user's request ("can you revamp the 404 to match the digital portal design system"): this host is the portal, so the page every wrong address on it lands on had no business reading as somewhere else. It is the cover this portal gives "Link not recognised" — the mark on a bar of `--head-h`, the title, the line that says what to do rather than restating the title, and two small controls (`.btn-sm`: Visit website, Contact support) in the documented order at their own widths on a desk and as equal halves on a phone. **English only** since 2026-09-24 (the user: "for page 404, show only in english"; it had printed the Chinese beneath), white to the browser's edge like the front door, the title 17px and the line 14px. Built from `css/portal.css`, so it carries the version stamp and moves with the tokens. Three things went with the old page: a `noscript` redirect to adspacestudios.com (there because that page could not draw itself without script; this one needs none, so the redirect would only have thrown a reader off a page they could already read), and `/css/main.css` and `/fonts/Custom.TTF`, neither of which exists on this host. It is in `uxaudit`'s walk beside the front door.
- Root HTML files (`ap01.html`, `ap02.html`, `ap03.html`, `ap-dale.html`, `accv-new.html`, `3pform.html`, `einvoiceinfo.html`, `interview-quiz.html`, `sales-program.html`, `supplier.html`) are the user's existing site. Never edit them.
- Portal pages are folders with an `index.html` and clean paths (`/admin/`, `/creators/`, `/review/`), never `.html` in a URL. New pages start from `docs/PAGE-TEMPLATE.html`.
- One stylesheet `css/portal.css`; one script per section in `js/`; `js/api.js` is the only Supabase client; `js/money.js` the only money formatter; `js/chrome.js` the only header and footer; `js/menu.js` the only copy of where a row ⋯ opens and what closes it; `js/copy.js` the only copy of what a Copy button says when it has copied (four buttons each said it differently: one swapped its label, one a span inside itself, one wrote into a `.msg` line, one tinted itself); **`js/words.js` the only copy of a word two pages share** (loaded before every page script); **`js/group.js` the only copy of a directory group** (the heading that folds, its count, the card with its header row and the Show more); **`js/sheet.js` the only copy of how a form sheet opens, shuts and refuses to throw typed work away**; **`js/form.js` the only copy of a segment and a More details fold** (a `select[data-seg]` drawn as a radio group, the select kept as the source of truth; a `details.fmore` whose line says what it holds); **`js/cmdbar.js` the only copy of what a command bar becomes on a phone** (the Filters button, its badge, the sheet the selects come up in, the ⋯ that holds a second action); **`js/state.js` the only copy of how a list says it is loading, has nothing in it, or could not be read** (three files had written those three states four different ways, and one of the four reported a failed read as an empty list). No build step, no framework, no bundler, ES5-style function scripts wrapped in an IIFE.
- **Server-side code that is not a Supabase edge function lives in `workers/`**, one folder per Worker, with its source and a README naming the account, the zone, the Worker, the custom domain and the three variables. `workers/links/` is the `hi.adspace.me` redirector. It is deployed from the repository and is not part of the Pages build.
- Docs for setup live in `docs/` (`CONTENT-REVIEW-SETUP.md`, `S3-UPLOAD-SETUP.md`, `S3-STORAGE.md`, `DRIVE-IMPORT-CHECK.md`, `FIX-ACCESS-DENIED.md`, `CREATOR-UPLOAD-CHECK.md`, `OPERATIONS-SETUP.md`, `OPERATIONS-MIGRATION.md`, `GOOGLE-MEET-SETUP.md`, `PERFORMANCE-SETUP.md`).
- **The portal writes to S3 and never removes anything** (`docs/S3-STORAGE.md`, 2026-09-21). An **orphan** — an object no row points at, left by a failed save or a deleted client — is invisible to the portal and billable for ever, and an abandoned multipart upload is billable and invisible even in the object list. The answer in order of value: **a lifecycle rule in two halves, applied at different times** (2026-09-21) — the housekeeping half now (abort incomplete uploads after 7 days, `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` at 30), because an abandoned 1 GB upload is billable storage that never appears in the object list and is a fifth of the Free Tier's 5 GB; the **storage-class half deliberately not yet**, because the Free Tier covers S3 **Standard only**, so on a small bucket a transition moves data out of what is free into what is billed and adds a per-request charge, a 30 day IA minimum and a per-GB retrieval fee to save a fraction of a cent per GB. Standard-IA at 90 and Glacier Instant Retrieval at 365 are added once the bill shows a storage line worth reducing, in practice past about 100 GB or when the Free Tier's twelve months end. **No expiration action at any size**, because a client asking for last year's reel and being told it is gone is worse than the bill. The first version of this doc recommended the transitions unconditionally, which was wrong at the volume this portal actually holds; **deleting an object when its row goes**, which is not built and needs a predicate that reads `campaign_deliverables.file_url`, `campaigns.invoice_url`, `clients.logo_url`, `drive_assets.url` and — the awkward one — **inside `posts.media`, a jsonb array of `{url, type, poster}`**, with a soft-removed deliverable counting as still in use because its Undo restores the row; and **splitting the IAM identity** so the portal's key may only `s3:PutObject` under `content/` and gains `s3:DeleteObject` only when that delete path ships. A key that cannot delete cannot be made to delete.
- **A change to one database function ships as a file in `supabase/migrations/`, not as a re-run of the whole schema.** `supabase/schema.sql` carries fifteen top-level data migrations (team roles and their defaults, the rate card minimums and inclusions, client slugs, the stage clock backfill, the team stand-down repair, the Marketing and rednote renames) and drops and recreates fifty-six policies, triggers and indexes. Every one of those is idempotent and several are guarded, but re-running all of it on a live database to replace one function body is unnecessary exposure. A migration file is dated, narrowly scoped, safe to run twice, carries its own rollback, and is applied standalone by `tests/sql.js`.
- Secrets never enter the repo. The Supabase anon key and the Google browser key are public by design and held back by their restrictions (Google key: websites `digital.adspace.me/*`, Drive API only). The delete code lives in the database.

### Infrastructure and assets (established, do not re-ask)
- Hosting: GitHub Pages, custom domain digital.adspace.me. Cloudflare Pages (`adspace-form.pages.dev`) only builds PR previews; the move to Cloudflare Pages was tried and abandoned (Access Denied), the site stays on GitHub Pages.

Older `ADspace.png` and the website favicon were rejected.
- Issuer (`ADSPACE_ORG` in `js/config.js`, entered by the user): ADSPACE PLT, registration 202304002162, SST J31-2401-32100002, 61-02, Jalan Mutiara Emas 2A, Taman Mount Austin, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia, advertise@adspacestudios.com, 60187625233 (printed as (60)18 762 5233), adspacestudios.com. Bank line still blank.
- Emails: support and issuer advertise@adspacestudios.com, account manager marketing@adspacestudios.com, admin login adspacestudios@gmail.com. Terms https://adspacestudios.com/legal/policies.
- Short links: new links are written under `ADSPACE_CONFIG.linkHost` (`hi.adspace.me`); `go.adspace.me` stays alive for the Rebrandly QR codes already printed on slides, which encode the whole address. About 50 slugs on Rebrandly. No redirector is built for either host yet.

### Behavioural guardrails the user gave (verbatim spirit)
- "This should be automatic on your structure when designing." Every rule in `DESIGN.md` is applied before the user sees a screenshot, never after.
- "Do not state the obvious." "Be concise and direct." No explanatory copy anywhere.
- "Return means go back." Back for navigation, Revert for a state, Restore for a record, Reinstate for a person.
- "Every action needs a way back." Nothing is deleted by one click; soft remove, Undo, Void then Delete.
- "Big card for short messages": a message is a line, not a card.
- "Same status throughout": the console and the client page use one vocabulary and one colour set.
- "Prefilled, not fixed": catalogue values seed a line and stay editable.
- "A phone screenshot is reviewed, not just taken."
- "Why do I need to fill in the handles here": intake asks for what is known on day one only.
- "Not AI SaaS": flat, quiet, corporate, Apple and Cloudflare register.
- "Memory like a goldfish": when a rule is learned it is written here the same push, with the section it belongs to, so it never has to be repeated.
- **Write to the user in corporate register: short, concise, straightforward, instructions first.** This governs the replies in the chat, not only the copy on the screen. No literary sentences, no narration of the reasoning, no essay where a list will do: what changed, what it means for them, what they have to do. Asked for several times before it was written down, which is the failure this line exists to stop.

The decisions: **A** a content task's row shows its real stage and a stage select; **B** the published filters are back (In progress, Due soon, AQC review, Client review, Waiting on client, Late); **C** Group by stage, keeping status; **D** the head's meta does not repeat the format; **E/F** the words (Task Owner, Created by, Bulk add, `#WT00001`); **G** skipping a step is ops Work with a reason, as published, superseding the earlier tightening to Manage. The structure: the list stays and a task opens in the portal's own side sheet of layered cards, the full record one press further; blue only for a hand-off; the Task Owner changed on the step by an unticked tick; the timer off the default path. Added from the review: **the draft link is optional** ("we have a WhatsApp group"): the step reads Sent on WhatsApp and records it, and the database takes the link or a note; **every added thing has edit, delete and Undo, and every stage a Revert** ("check if all comes with edit / delete / revert"); the card actions follow the design system (a quiet action per card opening a small form, one filled action at a time). **Two migrations to run by hand, in this order**: `supabase/migrations/2026-09-24-my-work-daily-tasks.sql` (mirrored in `supabase/schema.sql`, statements and header compared by `tests/ops.js`), then `supabase/migrations/2026-09-24-clear-test-tasks.sql`, once and on purpose, because it deletes the test tasks and resets the numbering. And the SOP's stage names were cut off in the 124px state column ("Performance r", "Revision (Inter"): the task row's stage track is 160px and every state select ends a longer name in an ellipsis; on a narrow list the stage jumped between lines by the words in the row, and now keeps one place; between 640 and 860 the list's task name was squeezed to 64 to 108px, and the list now states its own narrow line (`data-narrow`, read by `ADspaceState.fit`). Known limit: a Revert back into a review counts as a new round, because the round is counted off the moves into that stage. Verified by `ops: ok`, `sql: ok`, `work: ok`, the sweep, `matrix: ok` and `uxaudit: ok`.

Verified by `ops: ok`, `sql: ok`, `work: ok`, `crm: ok`, the sweep, `matrix: ok` and `uxaudit: ok`.

- **2026-09-15** — Creators sign in with an eight character code rather than an account or an SMS one time code. - **2026-09-15 — approved, NOT YET BUILT.** A creator's submission goes to the team before it goes to the client. `creator_submit` currently sets the step straight to `reviewing`, which on the client's page reads "Your approval": the chip asks the client to act the moment the creator uploads, while `campaign_deliverables` is team-only, so there is nothing there for them to open and the buttons only draw when somebody has separately pasted a `draft_url`. A **Submitted** step goes between `pending_draft` and `reviewing`. The client reads Submitted as "Draft in progress", because nothing has reached them. The team then either **releases to the client**, which is what exposes the creator's uploaded file URLs to the client-facing function so the client opens the creator's own files and the Drive folder leaves the loop, or sends it back to the creator as Changes requested with a note — an internal round the client never sees. Decided with the user on 2026-09-15; its own branch and PR, after the upload fix merges.

- **2026-09-22** — The state lives in the record head's right part beside the ⋯ on both records: the campaign's chip and the client's stage select. The client portal's rail is excluded from the split because its rows key on the rail's own width class.
- **2026-09-21** — The client record's **Key dates block is the Timeline**, and it is the one place every date and every duration lives. The stage journey is a row per stage (when it began, how long it ran) above a rule, the dates the record holds are below it, and the stage that is running carries the weight and the overdue mark. **The Account status block is gone**, superseding the 2026-09-21 decision that the rail opens on it: with the clock moved here, the block repeated the stage select the head already carries. The journey's mute line under Details is gone for the same reason. Each stage row is a turnaround the team asked to be able to average later (speed to first contact, contact to proposal, proposal to close, how long engaged) and **nothing new is stored for any of it** — `stage_log` has been stamped since the clock shipped, so a report across every client needs no field and no backfill. **Client since is edited in place**: the value becomes the picker and the pen beside it becomes the tick (`ADspaceAsk.rename`, extended once with `type` and `value` so a date can seed its field differently from the words on the row); the separate field and Save button are gone. Verified by `node tests/crm.js tests` → `crm: ok`, `uxaudit: ok`, `matrix: ok`.

Declined, each by a rule already recorded here: a page title with a blurb (explanatory copy; the bar names the route), a Status column with a dot and Active on every row (the accent marks the exception), the group as a column on every member (headings, decided 2026-09-16), and an access summary per member (`Clients + 4 more` hides four of five facts and repeats the group's access per person). The flat register without a bounded panel is a portal-wide decision across every register and the record panes, not a page at a time, and has not been made.

The Team panel folds each section's parts under its own head, taken from the Bukku permissions screen the user showed; Bukku's level codes and per-state scope ticks were not taken. **Own clients only** (a row scope for Sales under Clients) was raised and is its own batch, not built.
- **2026-09-19** — The operations system's Phase 1 (the data model, the read rules and the server functions) is in `supabase/migrations/2026-09-19-operations-system.sql`, mirrored byte for byte in `supabase/schema.sql`. **Its permissions are the existing access ladder**, not the seven booleans the brief named: `ops` View/Work/Manage for use, create and assign, and `ops.all`, `ops.reports`, `ops.workflows`, `ops.time` for the team queue, reports, templates and another person's hours. **The four parts are granted, never inherited** (`ops_granted()`), because each widens what the section opens rather than narrowing it, and an inherited widening makes the safe configuration the one somebody has to remember. Decided against a parallel boolean system on the ground that two authorisation systems is a data-integrity defect (§2 priority 1), and reported to the user with the mapping.
- **2026-09-19** — Operations writes are security-definer functions only; the `ops_` tables carry a select policy and nothing else, so a browser cannot set a stage, a date, an assignment, a completion or an event. The one direct write is marking your own notification read. `expected_version` refuses a stale write with the current row. Original commitments are written once. Cycle time, stage time and active work are three separate measures and are never summed. Verified by `node tests/ops.js tests` → `ops: ok`.
- **2026-09-19** — My Work is built for about 290 tasks a month (eight contents a week across thirty clients), so: **the read is bounded and open work is not part of the bound** (open work in full however old, finished work from a chosen period, the period select drawn only while finished work can be on the page); **Group by** re-bands the same rows by due date, client, stage or owner, with every card shut off the due axis so the page is headings and counts, the heading carrying the overdue count a shut card would hide; the fold is remembered per axis (`ADspaceGroup.section`'s new `memo`, which separates a card's identity from what its fold is filed under); and **a stage moves from the row** through the same function and gates, which is why the row is no longer a single button — the name cell opens the record instead. Three global corrections went with it: `.rectabs` no longer bleeds past the page gutter on a phone, the step under a tab strip has one owner (the strip, at 12px, as `.tabrow` already did), and the `?` no longer inherits the action's `margin-left: auto`. - **2026-09-21 — S3 storage, stated; step 1 is the user's to apply.** `docs/S3-STORAGE.md`. The portal writes to S3 and never removes anything, so orphans (an object no row points at) and abandoned multipart uploads are billable for ever and invisible to the portal. **Step 1, the lifecycle rule, is two halves applied at different times** (corrected 2026-09-21, after the user asked whether it would cost them their Free Tier — it would have). Apply the **housekeeping half now**: abort incomplete uploads at 7 days and `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` at 30. It is worth doing for the leak it stops, not the money it saves — an abandoned 1 GB upload is billable and invisible in the object list, a fifth of the Free Tier's 5 GB. **Hold the storage-class half**: the Free Tier covers S3 **Standard only**, so a transition on a small bucket moves data out of what is free into what is billed and adds a per-request charge, a 30 day IA minimum and a per-GB retrieval fee to save a fraction of a cent per GB per month. Add Standard-IA at 90 and Glacier Instant Retrieval at 365 once the bill shows a storage line worth reducing (past roughly 100 GB, or when the Free Tier's twelve months end). **No expiration action at any size** — cheaper, never deleted. The lesson: a cost optimisation is sized against the actual bill before it is recommended, or it is a recommendation to spend money. **Step 2, delete on remove, is NOT built** and is deliberately not rushed: it is irreversible, and the predicate it needs is not one column (`posts.media` is a jsonb array of `{url, type, poster}`, and a soft-removed deliverable counts as still in use because Undo restores it). **Step 3, the IAM split, is NOT built**: the portal's key should hold `s3:PutObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::myadspace/content/*` and nothing else, gaining `s3:DeleteObject` only when step 2 ships, because a key that cannot delete cannot be made to delete. Rotation is add the second key, redeploy, confirm an upload, then delete the first — never the other order.
- **2026-09-21 — the delay rule, built.** A task past its `current_final_due_at` and still short of a stage whose `stage_group` is `client_review` is **late**, whatever its own stage says; one that reached review met the promise and is not. Derived on every read (`isLate()` in `js/ops.js`, off `reviewFloor()` which reads the workflow's own stages), never stored. The warn paint on the queue row, the board card and the rail's commitment row now means *late* rather than *the date has passed*, because the accent marks the exception; the cell's words still state the days over either way. A **Late** option in the stage filter is the view a manager opens, a filter and not a band because it cuts across every stage. `tests/work.js` proves the distinction against a fixture that is past its date *at* client review, which is the only thing that tells the rule apart from the old one.
