- **2026-10-01 — Draft with AI in the house style.** The first live press failed: the model the user set refuses a forced `tool_choice` (400), so the four fields are now held by structured output (`output_config.format`), with room for the model to think first, and every refusal is logged with the API's own reason and named on the page (no credit, a model name not known). The user then shared four approved ads reports to set the tone. They share one shape (a summary paragraph on spend, delivery, the objective and the strongest ad; What worked by objective with sub-points; What to fix with the reason; a focus with budget splits and the ads that continue), and their best lines rest on context the figures cannot carry: budget moved to Google Ads, a lead form made longer, ads paused, unspent budget carried forward, next month's budget. So the house style is written into the function (with an invented example, since the repository is public), tightened where the reports were loosest (a reason and an action for every fix; cost per result compared only like with like; no "RM 0.00"), and the page gains Notes for the draft, sent with the press and kept only in the browser so it can never reach the client's copy. The client's last finished report's commentary is sent too, so a month follows up on what it promised, with the client's name masked as "the brand". The accounts report has the same button on its own fields. In the ads ranking the result's word now sits whole under its count (Post engagements had broken between letters in a narrow column), a one-month run reads 1 to 30 Sept 2026, and a cost under ten sen shows three decimals.
- **2026-10-01 — Meet clashes, the meeting sheet, the calendar's place.** The user: after Save the Content meeting sheet stayed open while the month behind it had already updated, and the date calendar opened at the window's top left; and the shared calendar holds other plans, so a Meet should be refused only where another meeting link overlaps. `meet-create` now counts only events carrying a Meet link or a Meet, Zoom or Teams address (the sheet had stayed open because Google answered `slot-taken` for an ordinary event, and its reason sat under Led by, below the sheet's fold; a refusal now scrolls its line into sight). The DD/MM/YYYY box's hidden calendar field now takes the box's own place and size, and its layout is read before `showPicker`, because Safari anchored a first open to where the 1px field had last been laid out.
- **2026-10-01 — Accounts report read platform by platform; captions as written; the foot on the margin.** The user, from a live PDF: findings combined across platforms confuse ("all platforms algo work differently"), the Top posts page ranked every platform's posts together beside each platform's own top five, captions came out crumpled with blanks where the emoji were, the Draft line lifted the foot, and Post engagements broke between letters. The accounts report now reads Executive summary, then Insights and recommendations with one block a platform (its line, Highlights, Areas to improve, Recommendations, from the account's own fields), then each platform's page with its top three posts ranked on that platform alone (`topOf`) as cards carrying the figures, the caption on its own lines and the remarks; the mixed ranking page is gone. The Commentary step edits all of it in one place: the summary, each platform's four fields and its top posts' Why it stood out; the old across-platform fields stay in a fold so older reports lose nothing. Draft with AI answers the same shape, in a more formal client-facing voice, with platform-specific reasoning allowed only as recommendation. The blanks were a timing fault: emoji images were embedded after the pages were drawn, so every emoji is now embedded first. The foot's Draft or version line is removed and the foot sits on the margin's line. Post engagements reads Engagements everywhere (a second paste still matches rows stored under the old word, through `resultWord`).
- **2026-10-01 — Draft with AI is rate limited in the database.** The user asked for a limit on drafting. Every press is claimed through `ai_draft_claim` before Claude is asked: 5 a report, 20 a colleague, 60 the team in any 24 hours, counted under one advisory lock so two presses cannot both take the last; a press that fails is marked failed by `report-draft` (`ai_draft_done`) and not counted, so an outage does not use up the day. The count lives in `ai_drafts` (RLS on, no policy, every grant revoked), not in the browser, so it cannot be cleared from a page. The user also floated one free draft then an admin master code for the rest; recommended against a shared code (it travels and cannot say who used it) in favour of these per-person caps, with the console's monthly spend limit as the hard ceiling.
- **2026-10-01 — One draft a report; again is an admin's.** The user chose it over the master code: a colleague who is not an admin has one draft a report (a failed one does not count), and an admin drafts it again, to 5 a report in 24 hours; the per-person and team caps stand. Keyed on the login (`team_members.is_admin`), so nothing is shared or passed around.
- **2026-10-01 — Each ad row keeps its Ad IDs.** The user saw two ads with no results and could not tell which ads in Ads Manager they were, and was still dating ads by hand. An export's Ad ID and Account ID columns are now kept on the row (`sm_report_ads.ad_ids`, `ad_account`): the IDs show under the name as copy controls, the ⋯ opens the account in Ads Manager with those ads chosen, and a second paste (a day export for the dates) matches rows by Ad ID before the name. A blank result is Meta's own: the ad had no results of that type in the period. The IDs are the team's reference and never reach the PDF.
- **2026-10-01 — A paid draft is never lost; the ads PDF reads tighter.** The user asked that leaving mid draft warn, since the tokens are spent. Closing or reloading the tab mid draft now asks (the browser's own question; a page cannot word it), and moving to another step or screen inside the console no longer loses anything: the answer is kept for its report and filled in on return, so no in-console warning is needed. In the ads PDF a result reads as a count and one short word (47 Leads, 15 Messages, 84,660 Reached), never Ads Manager's long name broken mid word, and an ad that spent with no result reads 0 Leads (the user changed None to this the same day; one result reads 1 Lead), the console rows reading the same short word; Interactions and Reactions keep their own words so two result types are never shown as one. Points in the commentary tables move whole to the next page. Each objective's ads are listed in the console as the PDF ranks them. A top post card no longer repeats its date under a name that already carries it, and its figures run the column's width.
- **2026-10-01 — A creative card carries each objective's spend, under a table head.** The user found the card's labels and figures hard to tell apart (both small, Book and Regular) and asked whether the spend per objective belongs on it. It does: the card's head states the creative's total, and each line's cost per result is read against its own spend, so each line now has Amount spent. The labels sit on the shaded band in Slate Regular that every other table in the report uses. The ranking table and the cards stay: the table ranks the ads within an objective, the card reads one creative across objectives with its age split and video figures.
- **2026-10-01 — Drafts in Chinese, shorter, and never against our own work.** The user asked for Chinese clients and found drafts long and, worse, critical of the content, planning and creatives the agency itself made, which undermines the client's confidence. A language segment (English / 中文) sits beside Draft with AI, prefilled from the main contact's preferred language and kept per client; Chinese is composed as Chinese, not translated. Every draft now keeps to a few points a field and one sentence a point, and reads a shortfall as what the audience showed and what we will test next, never a fault in our work. The ads report's What to fix is now Areas to improve, as on the accounts report. A fully Chinese PDF (headings and labels) is a separate step, not done.
- **2026-10-01 — Preview before Issue; a letter is never lost to a stray click.** The user asked to see a document before issuing it and found the Issue document sheet closed on a click outside it, losing the letter. Preview draws the sheet as it stands on the letterhead without writing anything or spending a number (reference PREVIEW). The register's own sheets had their own outside-click handler that ignored the rule every other sheet keeps; they now close on it only while untouched. A save-as-draft for letters was not built: Preview answers the need to check before issuing without a second state to manage.
- **2026-10-01 — A client letter is ACL/{Client ID}/{YYMMDD}{NN}.** The user set the reference for a letter to a client: ACL (ADspace Cover Letter), the Client ID, the date as YYMMDD and the day's index from 01. `issue_document` builds it from the letter's own date (today unless the sheet gives another, so a dated letter and its reference agree), takes the lowest number free for that client that day, and holds an advisory lock on the base so two issuers cannot take one number. The engaged `SA/` distinction and the type code are dropped from new references; letters already issued keep theirs and /verify/ answers both (`2026-10-01-client-letter-serial.sql`).
- **2026-10-01 — Signed or not is a tick on the letter.** The user asked whether a computer-generated letter needs signing and chose a tick per letter over changing types. To be signed is prefilled from the type; unticked, the issuer is still named (straight under ADSPACE PLT, no signing space) and the foot says no signature is required. `issue_document` takes `p_signed` (the twelve-argument shape dropped first, `2026-10-01-letter-signature-tick.sql`).
- **2026-10-01 — Overview reads a section at a time.** The user found the Overview one long scroll and asked for the tabs and swipe the other pages use. Each section is a tab over its own pane, counting what its list cards hold and warn where something is late, so the glance across sections survives in the strip. It opens on the first tab rather than jumping to a late one once the counts arrive, which would move the page under the reader; the warn count points at it instead.
- **2026-10-01 — A report can be issued in Chinese.** The user asked for Chinese clients, in professional corporate Chinese and never word for word, then narrowed it: the cover and the file name stay English (the report is known by one name), the titles and table heads inside read Chinese. The language is the report's own (`sm_reports.lang`), set beside Draft with AI and taken first from the main contact's preferred language, so the draft and the PDF always agree. Every fixed string of the PDF is answered from one hand-written dictionary at the drawing primitives, counts read with their measure words (47 个潜在客户) and dates as 2026年9月1日 (7月5日至6日 in a table cell, the year being the report's). The Chinese face moved from Noto Sans TC to SC, since a Simplified report on the Traditional subset can miss glyphs. Spreadsheet pastes now read quoted cells, so a caption copied with its line breaks keeps them.
- **2026-10-01 — In a Chinese report the template stays English.** On the first Chinese PDF the user asked that only the context and table titles read Chinese and the template stay English: Executive summary, Insights and recommendations, Ad performance and every page title, the header and the foot. The page titles and the furniture are drawn with the Chinese layer off; table titles, column heads, notes and dates stay Chinese. A table's period sits on one line (7月12日至18日), the year being the report's.
- **2026-10-01 — Ad IDs open on a press; the commentary reads one way in both reports; titles in title case.** The user found eighteen-digit Ad IDs listed under every ad "a whole mess" and asked for a small control that opens them, and for them in the Edit ad sheet beside Cancel and Save. A row and the sheet's foot now name how many (2 Ad IDs) and open a card listing each as a copy control, with Copy all (comma separated, as Ads Manager's search takes them) and Open in Ads Manager. From the PDF: the ranking table's narrow Ad column broke 2608W4_OldOwnorInvest mid word while the figures had room to spare, so the name now takes the widest column, and an ad with no result shows a dash rather than Not available. The accounts report's insights were a label column beside the points; they now read as the advertising report does, a shaded head over numbered points. The report is a formal document, so its page titles and block heads take title case. The user also asked how the tables are ordered: each objective's ads cheapest cost per result first, those with no result after by spend; the creative cards below are a separate read, the creatives by total spend, most first.
- **2026-10-01 — The language switch is the draft's; the PDF stays English; new ad reports compare with the month before.** On a Chinese PDF the user found it read like a mainland report, while Meta's own terms are English and their clients read the commentary, not the labels, in Chinese. They had switched to 中文, drafted, switched back and exported, and asked that this be the behaviour: the switch now decides only the language Draft with AI writes in; the template, headings and labels print in English, and the commentary prints as written. The Chinese layer of the PDF is kept but switched off. The user also asked that First month of ads not be ticked by default, since most clients advertised before the portal: a new report starts unticked, and with no earlier report the month before is prefilled for its figures, which the team types from Ads Manager; a client's true first month is ticked by hand. On a running client, a finished September report's period and totals carry into October by themselves. The late count on the Overview tabs became a small warn chip: bare warn ink measured 4.50:1 on the tab track.
- **2026-10-01 — The Chinese face is TrueType in the repo, embedded as a subset.** Two Chinese PDFs from the user drew garbled in a strict viewer and weighed 7.4 MB. The face came from a CDN as OpenType with CFF outlines; pdf-lib cannot subset CFF and embedded the whole 8 MB face, declaring it TrueType (CIDFontType2, FontFile2) though it is not, which lenient viewers forgive and strict ones do not. The same Noto Sans SC 2.004 (OFL) was converted to TrueType outlines with fontTools and committed under css/. A first conversion still drew gaps: fontkit's subsetter joins glyphs without padding and writes short offsets, so any glyph of odd length shifts every one after it; the face is saved with its glyphs padded. A page of Chinese now adds about 10 KB, and letters with a Chinese block draw from the same face.

### 2026-10-01 · On a phone a sheet is pulled down to close, and a half-filled form is kept
From the UX brief's batch 2, the one item the user approved ("Sheet swipe-down + drafts"): swipe down to close, backdrop tap to close, and a draft of a half-filled sheet restored on reopening. The pull starts only on the sheet's head (a grabber drawn there), so a body that scrolls is never fought; past 90px or flicked, it presses the sheet's own close mark, so each section's own way out runs. A draft is kept against the exact state the sheet opened in (every field's value, hidden ids included), so an Edit of another record, or of a record changed since, is another form and restores nothing; only the fields the person changed by hand are kept, never the section's own filling. Pressing the sheet's action ends the draft whether the save succeeds or not: a failed save keeps the sheet open with its fields, and a saved Add must never fill the next one (a duplicate record). Because the typing is kept, the scrim closes a touched form sheet on a phone; a desk keeps no drafts and keeps the rule that the scrim never closes a touched form, where a stray click is rarer and the suites' Cancel-and-reopen paths stay as they were.

### 2026-10-01 · The Handbook: the internal files in the console, behind a minute-long link
The user asked whether the Employee Handbook and other internal files (SOPs, policies, templates) belong in the portal rather than an HRMS app, then chose to build it here: named Handbook, no read-and-accept step, admins alone edit. The portal already holds the team's sign-in, the activity record and the permission checks, so a file gains an audit trail and nothing to sign into twice; acknowledgement, leave and payroll stay with an HRMS if one is taken up later. The files sit in a private Supabase Storage bucket rather than S3: S3 is public through CloudFront and keeps everything, while a policy document must be readable only by a colleague who is signed in, and must be removable when it is withdrawn. A file is opened through a signed link that lasts 60 seconds, made at the press, so a copied address stops working a minute later. A version is a new object and a new row, never an overwrite, so the version a colleague read can always be shown. Archive is the soft remove; Delete takes the title typed back. The Handbook is not an access section with levels: every colleague reads it, and an admin's flag is the only write.

### 2026-10-02 · Audit after the October features: PDF libraries on demand, four fixes
The full walk at 1280 and 390 (both themes), a field scan of every input, the database calls each route makes on load, and console boot timing at a phone's CPU speed. Performance: pdf-lib and fontkit (1.1 MB) loaded in the head of the console and the client portal on every visit and cost about 600 ms of a phone's load; they are now fetched on the first drawing (`ADspaceDocs.lib()`), and first paint went from 796 ms to 284 ms, DOMContentLoaded from 1177 to 666 ms (4× CPU, warm). Database calls per route showed no waste: Overview's seven `ops_report` calls are the six-month trend, My Work's three task reads are open and finished work. Fixes: the closed rail drawer cast its shadow as a grey band down every phone screen's left edge (the shadow now belongs to the open drawer); Team's bar ⋯ took the small button's 92px minimum and stood apart from Add member (it is the bar's 32px square, as My Work's); the lead form's Industry used the filter idiom, so a new lead showed a blank select and Not set saved the word "all" (no live client held it); four email fields for other people (contact, finance, colleague) offered the signed-in person's own address and no longer autofill. Considered and left: `defer` on the console's own 41 scripts (a smaller gain against a boot order every suite depends on) and one read of `clients` for Overview's five cards (each card asks its own permission first).

### 2026-10-02 · Posts imported from a Meta export read as Meta writes them
The user imported a Facebook page's September export and got 330 posts dated 9 January, each titled with its caption: the importer read 09/01 day first, took Title as the name (Meta fills it with the caption) and made a post of every row of the daily export (one row per post per day). Meta's exports are month first, so a paste carrying Post ID and Publish time is read month first, and any other paste decides by its own dates (a part over 12 says which), falling back to day first as Malaysia writes. One Post ID is one post. Asked whether to download the lifetime export or have the daily one added up: both are taken. Lifetime carries Views and Reach and is taken as it is, but counts to the day it is downloaded, so it is the one to use when downloaded on the 1st of the next month; the daily export has no Views or Reach, its days inside the report's period are added up, and reach stays blank because people reached on two days are counted once, not twice. A re-import matches posts by their link and refreshes them. The bad rows already imported are cleared with Select on the Posts step (asked for the same day), which ticks posts and removes or moves them with Undo, as the Ads step does.

### 2026-10-02 · Invoice PDFs behind five-minute links
The user asked whether the S3 short-lived links ("batch 2" of the Documents register) had been built: they had not. Of the two scopes offered they chose documents only, since signing every media file would touch every page that plays a video. The one document the portal stores on S3 is a campaign's invoice PDF; letters and reports are redrawn on Download and never stored. A new invoice is now signed under `private/` (`sign-upload` with `private: true`, the console only, a PDF only), the row keeps the key, and `sign-download` hands a link that works for five minutes, finding the file from what the caller may already read: the campaign row read with a colleague's own token, or what `get_campaign` gives the client's link (which withholds the invoice until a creator is confirmed). The browser never names a path. An older invoice keeps its public address, because moving it would mean deleting the original and nothing deletes from S3; Remove PDF and upload again closes one. The code ships behind `privateInvoices` (off) because the bucket needs two hand steps first (the upload key may write and read `private/`; a bucket-policy deny shuts every other reader out of it); the switch is turned on once the user has done them. The user also asked about deleting the files the daily report names as unused: 18 files, 198 MB, about USD 0.005 a month. The report stays report-only, as the user decided on 2026-09-28.

### 2026-10-03 · Content Review and creator media behind a pass
After the invoices, the user asked that Content Review files and creator drafts go private too, worried a client or creator would open a review and find the video gone. Files are never moved or deleted, only the way in changes, so the worry is a link expiring under an open page. Signed URLs per file would have rewritten every media address on six pages and broken the browser's own cache with a new address each visit. CloudFront's signed cookies do neither: one policy over `content/*`, signed by `media-pass` after the page proves its review link, selection link, creator's code or sign-in (the same functions that answer those pages), set on `adspace.me` so `mycdn.adspace.me` receives them, for twelve hours. Every stored address and every link stays as it is. A file that fails with the pass gone asks again once and loads, a video from where it was, so a tab left open overnight recovers on its own; a refresh always does. The `.web.mp4` copy not yet made fails by design and never asks. The key pair is made by the function and kept in `app_secrets` (as the push keys are), so no private key passes through the chat; the user pastes the public half into CloudFront. The pass covers all of `content/` rather than one client's folder (a CloudFront policy holds one statement, and the selection page draws files from several folders): a raw address alone answers 403, and an address is a random UUID no page shows. Cost: no charge for signing; delivery as before through CloudFront, with the cache key free of cookies. Cut over in two steps so nothing breaks: the pages carry the pass first while CloudFront still answers everyone, then the `content/*` behaviour trusts the key group; undoing that one setting makes everything public again.

### 2026-10-06 · HR letters reach the colleague they name
The user asked whether a team member sees a letter issued to them, and chose: shared by default, a tick to keep a sensitive draft back, visible once issued, a notification, and only for letters issued to that person. ### 2026-10-06 · Every sliding strip measured, so a short strip cannot come back
The user, on an iPhone screenshot of My HR: "As always again? The sliding tab", then: "Seriously always found it but still repeatedly makes mistakes on this multiple times. Could you properly audit ALL sliding tabs". It was the third report of one fault: a strip stopping short of the card under it on a phone (the client portal's tabs on 2026-09-28, Content Review's stages on 2026-09-30, My HR's views now). Each fix covered one kind of strip, and the checks measured those strips by name, so a strip of another kind (here the Activity record's view strip, reused by Performance and My HR, which keeps its desk width) was never measured. The cause of the recurrence was the missing check, not the CSS alone.
The audit: a `strip` check in uxaudit's in-page checks, which matrix borrows, measures every strip on every screen of the walk at 1280 and 390 and at matrix's seven widths and 200% zoom. On a phone a strip must run the row it stands in, up to whatever shares its line; a record's strip, a strip inside a card and a report's steps must at every width; a strip that scrolls must fade an edge; the sliding surface must sit on the chosen option (segments too). The walk also lists every strip it meets and fails one on its list not met at both widths, or one it meets that the list does not name. Run on the code as it was, it found My HR's views 37px short at 390 in every state, and Performance's views 57px short of the padlock and gear at 200% zoom; every other strip passed. The census found three strips the walk had never reached: the reel and cover tabs on a client's review set (the walk read the demo set, which holds no pair), the Activity record's tabs (never opened), and a task record's tabs on a phone. The last was a fault in the walk itself: after Months, My Work holds two bars and two Filters marks, the walk's question about them threw, and on a phone it never reached a task at all, so the task's sheet, its record, its step sheet and its menus had never been measured at 390. The walk now presses the visible mark, opens the Activity record, and reads a review set with a pair.
The fix: a view strip standing on its own row (`.actstrip`) is the column's width on a phone with its views sharing what is spare, and beside the Performance tools it runs up to them.

### 2026-10-07 · Each published report keeps its PDF as it went out
The user: "if we keep adding or making changes to the pdf, does all created and completed ones still follow the previous or will follow the most latest version? ... if our client received version at (2026/10/06) but in the future maybe 2026/12/12 there is a new version, i no longer can fetch back the 2026/10/06 version only the latest one. is it the proper way of doing?" It was not: a published version kept its data (the frozen snapshot) but the file was redrawn on every download with the drawing of the day, so a later change to the PDF changed what an old download looked like, and the console offered no earlier version at all. Now, once a version is published, its PDF is drawn from that snapshot and stored once in the bucket's private folder for its client; every download of that version, the team's and the client's, hands over that file, read back as bytes through `sign-download` (never a link that could be forwarded), and the head's ⋯ Versions lists every version the client was given with its own Download. A version published before this, or whose first keep failed, is drawn from its own snapshot the next time anybody downloads it and kept then. A version taken off the portal and published again keeps the next file drawn, since its content may have been corrected in between. Stored on S3 rather than Supabase Storage: a report is about 1 to 3 MB, a few hundred a year cost cents on S3, and Supabase Storage's free allowance is shared with the Handbook. Nothing is ever deleted from the bucket, as before.

### 2026-10-07 · The stand-in hands a page fresh JSON, as PostgREST does
Testing the kept PDFs found the client's download and the Versions sheet handing over a newly drawn file rather than the one kept. The kept file's key was written, but the stand-in's stored copy stopped updating at that moment, so the next page load read the database from before it. The cause was in the stand-in, not the page: a read handed the page the stored row's own objects, the report engine notes its groups on the snapshot it draws (a reference back to the posts, which no JSON can hold), and from then every save of the stand-in's database failed in silence. PostgREST sends fresh JSON on every read and every function's answer, so the stand-in now does the same; a page changing what it read can no longer change, or break, the row.

### 2026-10-07 · The guide steps aside
The full gate on the guides found three faults before they shipped. The guide never opened by itself in the console: the Access denied cover, kept in its hidden shell, counted as an open cover, so every offer waited for ever; a layer now counts only when it is drawn. On the review page the guide took Escape while a post was open over it, so Escape no longer closed the post; now whatever is drawn over the page hears Escape first, and opening something over the guide (a sheet, a menu, a post) ends it as met, since the person has moved on. ### 2026-10-07 · Bold letters in a caption print as words
The user sent the appendix of an accounts report where a caption pasted from Instagram, 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗹, printed heavy and uneven. Those letters are not bold type: they are Unicode's mathematical letters (U+1D400 to U+1D7FF), which captions borrow to look bold. ### 2026-10-07 · Function hygiene: the Security Advisor's warnings
The user sent Supabase's Security Advisor: 0 errors, 430 warnings. Read against the live database, none was an open door: 257 were functions a signed-in caller may run (how the console works; each checks its caller), 135 functions with raised rights anon could run, 35 functions naming no search path (none with raised rights), pg_net in the public schema (Supabase cannot move it), leaked password protection (the portal has no passwords) and 34 notes on tables read only through functions. Of the 135, 53 showed no standard caller check; each was read: a public page's own function, a trigger (not callable), or a check of the caller's sign-in or grant inside. The user chose the tidy-up as a second lock. `functions_tidy()` names `search_path = public` on every function that names none, and takes EXECUTE from anon (and from PUBLIC, through which Postgres opens every new function) on every function with raised rights but those the public pages call, giving signed-in callers and the server back exactly what they had. The list of public functions is the one the schema already stated, its 28 grants to anon; the suite holds the two equal so the fact has one home. A function named by a policy anon meets would have stayed open (none is: every policy asking a function is for signed-in callers), and no edge function or page calls a closed function without a session: each edge function treats a refusal as denied. A function added later is closed by the next run, which every migration adding a function ends with.

### 2026-10-07 · Drafts are candid both ways, not only protective
The user, on the rules shipped the same hour: "the report could not also sound too protective for ourselves or way to beauty - eg. Totally no errors our services always perfect for continuously. It sounds fake and unreal as well as non realistic." The first pass had swung too far: it banned plain words such as underperformed and did not work, and offered comfort phrases in their place (room to grow, a clear signal for the next test, spend that showed us where to optimise next), which read as spin. The rule is now one of balance, so the good news is believed: the result is judged plainly and the work is never insulted. A shortfall is said with its figure, how far short and against what, and what we will change; a month weaker than the last is called weaker in the summary, not left to be found; a slip on our side that the notes name (a late launch, a broken link, an ad paused in error) is owned in one sentence with what was done; where the figures show no single cause the draft says so and names the test that will find out; a win is credited with its figure, never an adjective. `AVOID` now lists four kinds of words, English and Chinese: judgements of our work (bad, weak, boring, a mistake, wasted; 素材差, 失败, 浪费), praise no figure carries (excellent, outstanding, perfect, no issues, as always; 完美, 出色, 毫无问题, 零失误, 一如既往), comfort phrases in place of a figure (room to grow, valuable insights, a clear signal, positive momentum; 仍有提升空间, 宝贵经验), and words that colour a figure (only, unfortunately, thankfully; 仅仅, 遗憾, 幸好); plain words for a shortfall are given instead (lower, fell, fewer, cost more, did not reach, the least efficient; 下降, 低于, 未达到, 成本较高, 未达预期). The check gains a finding for a picture brighter than the figures: praise or certainty they do not carry, every ad said to have done well while one fell short, a fall told as good news, or a summary that reads as all good while a main figure got worse. The worked example now shows a weaker month called weaker, a shortfall stated against the strongest ad, and a cause the figures cannot show said so.

Its test caught that a mod may not submit a prompt beginning with `/`, so the buttons run the command (`$.command.run`). ### 2026-10-07 · One colour, one meaning: every primary blue, a status a dot and its word
Phase 1 of the colour revamp the user approved after the portal-wide colour audit ("Ok good / Looking forward to phase 2 and 3 as soon as"), on Apple's own guidelines. The audit counted five reasons a screen turned colour (an ink primary for our own progress, a blue primary for a hand-off, green, amber and red pills for states, an amber slab for caution, a red slab for destruction) and found most screens a wall of tinted pills in which nothing said what to press. One meaning a colour now. **Blue (`#0071E3`, apple.com's) is the one primary action of a view**, Add, Create and Save as much as Publish, Release and Approve: `.btn-primary` and `.btn-go` are one style. This supersedes 2026-09-16 (blue only for what moves work to somebody else, the ink fill for our own operations) and 2026-09-28 (the rewards confirmations ink, not blue): two primaries a reader had to tell apart answered a question nobody asks, and the word on the button already says whether it hands the work on. `#0071E3` carries white at 4.70:1; its hover and press are darker (`#0068D1`, `#005BB8`) because Apple's lighter hover falls to 4.32:1; `#007AFF` stays refused at 4.02:1; dark keeps the same blue under white, as apple.com does, and blue words take `--action-ink` (`#0066CC`, `#2997FF` in dark). **A status is a dot and its word in ink** (App Store Connect's own style): `.chip-state` and every toned chip lose their tinted ground, keep the word at 12.5/500 and take an 8px dot in Apple's system colours (`--dot-ok`, `--dot-wait`, `--dot-late`, `--dot-off`): green done or live, amber waiting on somebody or still running, red needs acting on now, grey not started, paused or closed. A stage select carries the dot inside its own box (`--sdot`), never a tint. A fact (High, Goodwill, White label, You) is the bare grey tag, never a status colour: it had been warn or green where it described rather than reported. **Three button roles, as Apple's**: the blue primary; the tonal button for everything else, caution included (`.btn-warn` is tonal now: Unpublish, Withdraw, Stop, Revert and Reopen cost nothing to look at, and the question each opens says what it costs); `.btn-danger` red words on the tonal button, never a red slab, which read as an alarm. **The stage tones follow the law**: ready to start is grey (not started), in progress and a revision amber (still running), waiting amber, cleared green, blocked red; Waiting on client, In production and the everyday In progress and Review the same. **What stays**: red for late and urgent and amber for waiting (2026-10-07, above) as dots; the announcement's Important and the upgrade line as the neutral band led by the amber dot rather than the warn pair; a tab's count red only where what it counts needs acting on now, a waiting or done count neutral; `.msg.warn` the words in ink after an amber dot; Health's pink and the calendar's purple in their one place each; chart bars over a guidance figure in `--warn`. The DESIGN.md register line "no coloured dots for status" is replaced: the dot is not decoration but the one colour a status keeps, always beside its word. Phases 2 (sizes that flow) and 3 (calm and elegant) follow as their own batches.

### 2026-10-10 · Pictures from Meta, and TikTok's campaign report

Reports showed an empty square for every imported post and ad: the team asked
for thumbnails without uploading each one. Import from Meta now asks Meta
for each ad's creative picture and each post's image or cover frame, and the
page keeps a 320px copy on the row. The pictures are fetched through
`meta-import`, never by the browser: Meta's image addresses expire within
days and cannot be read across origins. Only Meta's image hosts are fetched,
six a call. A picture the team chose is never replaced. The stand-in now
reads a `.is()` guard on an update against the row as it stood, as
PostgREST does; it had answered every guarded update with nothing.

The team's first TikTok export was a campaign report, not the ad level
export the importer was written for: no Ad name (Campaign name), Spend
rather than Cost, Conversions beside Results, CTR as a fraction, and a
Total of N results row last. The importer reads it as it comes. It carries

### 2026-10-10 · Audit fixes, batch 1: the gate, Confirmed, failures said, the worker's reach

An outside review (the user's second checker) found, and I verified on main,
gaps the gate itself let through. The gate passed a suite that printed a
FAIL before its last line, or nothing at all, and five suites only printed
what they saw. It now fails any FAIL line and an empty output, refuses to
test a server that serves another folder, and names the tests' commit; the
five suites assert. A suite that tests the gate's judgement joins it.

The service sheet still offered Confirmed and wrote it, though the line's own
control had refused it since the letter became the only way in. A trigger now
refuses a page writing Confirmed; `verify_letter` and the admin override run
as their owner and pass, so no function was restated. A configured review
page whose database library failed to load had shown demo posts and a
decision that was never sent; it now says it could not load. Refresh app
unregistered every page's worker on the browser; it now takes only the
console's own. A drawn PDF outlived its hour when read; the hour is kept on
every read and signing out lets go of the page's own. The client portal's
Request change moved onto the shared sheet, and a creator's unsent caption
is kept a booking.

Where the reviewer's fix was heavier than the problem, the lighter one was
taken: no structured result line in every suite, no build fingerprints.

A random file name is not an authorization boundary (the user, 2026-10-10):
the media pass over all of `content/` stays an open finding (F3) until
CloudFront's own configuration is read and the pass is tested against it.

A suite written for F6 and F7 (`tests/fileworker.js`, ten checks failing on
main) found the console worker's own clean-up deleting every cache but its
own whenever it updated; it now clears only the console's older stores.

### 2026-10-10 · A withdrawn notice can be deleted

The user, from the Notices list: "why notices cannot be deleted?" Notices were
built with Withdraw and Restore alone; nothing decided against a delete, and
announcements had gained one on the same question on 2026-10-07. A withdrawn
notice's row now keeps Restore and gains a ⋯ holding Delete, asked with the
notice named and no restore; `team_notice_delete` removes the notice and every
colleague's copy, refuses one still live (Withdraw first, so nothing leaves a
bell unseen), and files it under Notices. A push already on a phone stays.

### 2026-10-10 · The database is kept every night

The audit asked for backup and restore evidence; the user: "no backups for
supabase yet since its on freemium?", then "First use the free method"
rather than the Pro plan's daily backups. A GitHub Actions run each night
takes Supabase's own dump (the three files its restore guide uses: roles,
schema, data), refuses one that holds no clients, encrypts it with a
passphrase kept in the company's password manager, and puts it under the
bucket's `private/` with a key that may only add files there. It runs on its
schedule or by hand, never on a pull request, so a fork never reaches its
secrets; it lives in this public repository because only its secrets are
secret. A raw `pg_dump` was refused: Supabase's guide says its internals
break a restore. Handbook files in Supabase Storage are not covered.

### 2026-10-10 · An upload is signed only for its own purpose and record

The outside review (P1) found `sign-upload` signing an upload into any client
for any signed-in colleague, and a first fix let Work in any upload section
sign every kind. The user: "P1 must check the specific upload purpose, parent
record, section permission and client scope. Having Work permission in any
upload-capable section must not authorize every upload type." Each upload
now names what it is for and its record (a content set's file, a client's
logo, a booking's draft, a campaign's invoice, a report's kept PDF); the
function reads the record with the service role, checks it is the named
client's, then asks the database as the caller for that purpose's own
section or part at Work and the client scope. A report's PDF is always
private and a logo never. P2 in the same release: an email is matched as
itself in every edge function, so an address holding `_` or `%` never stands
for another's (`portal-login` had made logins on such a match).

The user asked for the theme to be set from the name menu, for that menu to
be smaller, and called the three marks at the rail's foot "so weird". The

Arrange sections (each only where it may be used); Theme,
Passkeys, Notifications and Refresh app; Sign out. Its rows are a control's
height at a desk (38px, the floor uxaudit's `target` holds) and 48px docked
on a phone; it is 272px wide. The Activity record, read more often, stays
at the rail's foot as one mark on the build's line (the user: "activity log
can go inline with version code", "just activity record icons would do"):
the build at the left and the mark at the right edge, at a desk as under

back except pressing to the device's register, and the bar now holds only

### 2026-10-10 · Confirming is one act a press

The audit found three acts that could happen twice or half (F1, S3, C1). On
the selection page a selection whose autosave the database refused could
still be confirmed with nothing in it, and a confirmation could be filed
against rates the client never saw. In the console Confirm creators was three
writes (the confirmation, each booking, the campaign) with no way back if one
failed. The portal's Request change filed a second request when a reply was
lost and the client pressed again.

Each is now one function, one transaction, with a key made once for the
press: `confirm_selection_with` (the creators on screen and the rate shown
for each, refused when either changed), `campaign_confirm_creators`, and
`portal_request_once`. The same key again answers with the first result and
files nothing. The older functions stay for pages loaded before, and
`confirm_selection` now refuses a selection that never saved. The audit's
remaining findings moved from the working ledger to STANDARD.md's open
findings, each removed as its batch closes it.

### 2026-10-10 · The client decides on what it saw, and keeps what it approved

The audit found four places where what the client saw and what was recorded
could part (F2, S5, S6, C2). A post edited after the review page opened could
still be approved, and the approval then stood over words the client never
read. A creator's next round, handed in after the client asked for changes,
showed on the client's page before the team had checked it. A file the
client had approved could be removed from the console at any state, and the
table's one policy let any colleague change its rows. A reply to a portal
request was written over a Withdraw the client made meanwhile.

The review page now sends the version it shows; a post changed since is
refused in the client's words and what was decided on is kept with the
decision. Release stamps the round released, and the client's page shows
that round alone; a file added while the booking waits for its quality
check voids the checks. From the client's approval on, the team hides a file
rather than removing it (the user: hide at Work; a permanent delete is an
admin's granted part alone, `campaigns.files_delete`, never implied by Full
Access; before approval Remove and Delete work as before). A request is
written only over the request as it was read. The guard trigger runs as the
caller: a security definer trigger sees its owner as `current_user`, so it
could never tell a page's write from a function's.

### 2026-10-10 · Letters held to their lines

The audit's fourth batch (S2, S4, R1). A Letter of Offer's totals were the
browser's: the database stored what the page sent, so a page could print one
figure and file another, and a line repriced while the sheet was open went
out at the old price. `issue_letter` now works the price from the stored
lines by the letter's own rule and keeps the page's figures only within a
sen (the browser's rounding), refusing anything further with its own. A
letter could also be verified after a line it printed was repriced or
removed, confirming terms the client never signed; `verify_letter` now
refuses both and the letter is reissued. `delete_client` left its record to
the page after the answer, so a lost reply left none; it files the deletion
itself. `client_documents` kept insert, update and delete policies no page
used; only the read stays.

The Activity record is not scoped by client, so the user's rule until it is:
a group seeing its own clients only holds no Activity access, refused in the
Team panel and by a trigger. Offboarding a colleague, a client's contact and
a client is written down in docs/OFFBOARDING.md.

### 2026-10-10 · A media pass per client folder

The audit's last finding (F3): the media pass opened every file under
`content/`, so a client holding a review link held a pass to every other
client's files, and a file name was the only boundary. CloudFront's signed
cookies carry one policy with one statement, so a pass is now one policy a
folder, each set on that folder's cookie path: a browser sends a folder's
pass to that folder alone. The review link opens its client's folder; the
selection link that and each booking's drafts; a creator their own bookings;
a client's contact each client they hold access at; a colleague all of
`content/`. A client page's pass takes away a whole-of-content pass an
earlier page left on the root. The folder layout is the one S3-STORAGE.md
records (`content/{clientId}/`, `content/creator/{optionId}/`), and nothing
changes in CloudFront.

The user may continue the portal from a team account once this one's credits
are spent; both reach the same repositories. A new session is given its own
branch, so `CLAUDE.md` no longer names one: it works on the branch it is
given, and a release in progress is carried by its PR (its description holds
the order and rollback, a comment what is still open), never by a session's
memory. Connectors (GitHub, Supabase) are per account and are connected again
there; no secret moves. Only one account works at a time, and "hand over"
(push both repositories, then one comment on the open PR) is the step
before switching.

### 2026-10-12 · Uploads refused by a second media pass
Add assets on Waringin read "Uploaded to S3, but nothing is served … 2 of 2
not uploaded". The files were stored and the console held a colleague's
pass asked a minute earlier (media-pass logs), yet the check that the CDN
serves the file failed on every try. Since passes per folder (audit F3,
2026-10-10) a client's review or selection link opened in the same browser
leaves its three cookies on that client's folder for twelve hours, beside
the console's on content/; the browser then sends two of each and
CloudFront refuses the file. The check read the file on a detached image,
which the media pass's own retry never hears, and blamed an Origin path
from the setup days. Now every pass keeps the folders it set in this
browser and the next pass takes them away; a file refused on a folder
another page left a pass on loads again once those cookies are gone; the
upload check asks for the pass first and once again before it refuses, in
words that no longer name an Origin path.

The same afternoon the user met the refusal again, from a console opened
before the deploy (the old words). S3 had answered 200 each time, so with
the media pass on the check no longer refuses a stored file: it asks for the
pass and reads once more, and the post is kept either way. Behind signed
cookies a refused read tells about the browser's cookies, not the
distribution, which was set up once and has not moved.

### 2026-10-14 · A WhatsApp message sent twice is asked about first
The user asked for a gate so that the same message is not sent twice when
one colleague missed that another had sent it, or forgot they had. Before a
send the composer asks the database for the newest message to that person
for that purpose and record within a window (24 hours, a Business setting,
`wa_repeat_hours`; 0 turns it off); found, Send asks again in warn naming
who sent it and when, with Send again. It warns rather than blocks: a
second send is sometimes intended (a lost message, a correction). `wa-send`
refuses the send unless that question was answered, so two colleagues
pressing at nearly the same moment are both asked. The function is
`wa_sent_recently`: `wa_recent()` already names the console's list of
recent messages.

- The user, 2026-10-15: every file under content/ in the console stopped
  loading ("its serious attention needed"; "This is the second time this

  `media-pass` answered 200 to every call, and with its pass each file
  loaded from mycdn.adspace.me (images, the .mov originals, their .web.mp4
  copies), without it 403; so the browser held the wrong cookies. The
  console's colleague pass covers /content/; a client link opened in the
  same browser (the team previewing Laman Citra's selection page) took
  that pass away and set its own folders, and the console's files then
  failed. The fix of 2026-10-12 had covered only the client page opened
  first, then the console.

  drawing on it; the console clears every folder a client page left each
  time it asks. `tests/mediapass.js` asserts the console-first order with a
  stand-in CDN that refuses none or two passes, and fails on the code
  before the fix.
- The lesson, in CLAUDE.md's guardrails: a fault between two pages is
  fixed and tested in both orders; a file that will not load is tested at
  its source (the pass and the CDN) before a page is blamed.

  inside `src` and `href` through an `esc` that left `"` alone, so an

  (`https://mycdn.adspace.me/content/creator/{booking}/{uuid}.{ext}`), a
  name of 1 to 255 and a kind the page sends; every page's `esc` that left
  out `"` or `'` (twenty-one copies) escapes both, and `ADspaceAsk.esc`,
  which escaped nothing and was used nowhere, is gone. Checked live: no
  stored file address or name holds a quote or an angle bracket; the three

  copies of `esc` are not merged here.

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: a creator's post link could carry script
  (security audit of 2026-10-16, finding 3). `post_link_ok` held the link

  `https://instagram.com/x"onmouseover="…` was stored and drawn as a link
  on the selection page, the console and the creator's page. It now

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: `sign-upload` signed any upload for a day
  (security audit of 2026-10-16, finding 4). It took any extension of five
  letters (html, svg and js included, served by the CDN from our domain),
  signed the PUT with no headers so the uploader chose its Content-Type,
  took the size on the caller's word, and left aws4fetch's own expiry of
  86,400 seconds. It now signs only the extensions the pages upload
  (videos, pictures, PDF, ZIP; the live store holds jpg, mov, png, mp4,
  jpeg and pdf), each with one type, and signs that type and the size
  claimed into the PUT (`allHeaders`, so S3 refuses another type or
  length) for 900 seconds; every page PUTs with the `contentType` it
  answers, and a creator's or the team's file with no extension in its
  name takes the one its type has. `S3_PREFIX` falls back to `content`,
  as the docs set it.

  (security audit of 2026-10-16, finding M, none closed by finding 2's

  `javascript://%0aalert(1)` as an address because it matched the scheme

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: the database read the UTC day (security audit of
  2026-10-16, finding A; the user: "all must in MYT"). The database's
  TimeZone is UTC, so `current_date` and `now()::date` were yesterday
  until 8:00am in Malaysia: on the 1st the new month and quarter were
  refused until then (`perf_today`, which every Performance rule asks), an
  issue logged that morning read as in the future, and My Work's late
  list counted a day late. Two ways were weighed. Setting the database's
  zone to Malaysia (one line) was refused: PostgREST writes every
  timestamp in the session's zone (`+00:00` today, which the pages read and
  compare as strings in places) and every `date::timestamptz` in the
  schema reads a day in it, so it would move stored-day arithmetic and the
  JSON every page reads. Instead each of the ten functions whose last
  definition read the server's day takes Malaysia's, as `health_today()`
  and most of the schema already did, and the three columns that default
  to today take Malaysia's day
  (`2026-10-17-malaysia-time-in-the-database.sql`). `tests/sql.js` reads
  the last definition of every function in the schema and fails on one
  that asks the server's day without the zone, whatever zone the machine's
  Postgres runs in.

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: a Letter of Offer made from a quotation could be
  priced differently from it (security audit of 2026-10-16, finding F).
  `quote_price` takes the term percentage once on the monthly subtotal and
  SST at the rate of the day it priced; `issue_letter` (and the page's
  `priceOf`) rounded each line's rate with its percentage before adding,
  and charged today's SST, so sen rates moved the letter by a sen or two
  and an SST change between the quotation and the letter moved it by the
  whole change. Where every line came from one quotation, the letter is now
  priced as the quotation was, its SST rate kept on the snapshot so a
  redraw prints the same (`2026-10-17-letters-priced-as-quoted.sql`,
  `js/documents.js`); every other letter is priced as before.
  `tests/lettersql.js` holds sen rates, an SST change, two terms and a
  mixed letter, and runs the page's own `priceOf` against the database.

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: a Write with AI run that used the model but gave no
  answer was free (security audit of 2026-10-16, finding G). Every daily
  limit counts the rows not marked failed, and the five edge functions
  marked a run failed whenever it ended without a usable answer: stopped
  at its length, refused, nothing parsable, a brand analysis out of turns.
  Those runs had cost tokens, and a run made to fail could be repeated
  without limit. The user's rule: "count every failure except rejected".
  A run whose tokens were kept (input above nought) is now `incomplete`,
  whichever of `ai_draft_done` and `ai_draft_tokens` arrives first
  (`2026-10-17-ai-runs-counted-as-they-ran.sql`); a request the API
  refused before generating keeps no tokens and stays failed. No edge
  function changed: each already keeps a run's tokens whenever the model
  answered.

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: a WhatsApp message could be sent twice (security
  audit of 2026-10-16, finding C). `wa-send` put a message back in the
  queue whenever its request to Meta failed, a connection that dropped or
  timed out after Meta had taken it included, and `wa_claim` took a row
  left at Sending for five minutes and sent it again; the queues were also
  woken only by the write that filled them. A send whose answer never came
  is now filed `unknown:` and kept as Not confirmed (`wa_outbox.state`
  `unknown`, trigger `wa_outbox_unknown`), never sent again by itself, and
  counts as Sent recently so a send by hand asks first; Meta's own refusal
  is still tried three times; each send gives up after 25 seconds so it is
  filed rather than cut off. pg_cron `outbox-drain` wakes both queues every
  five minutes while they hold something
  (`2026-10-17-whatsapp-sends-never-repeated.sql`).

- 2026-10-17 · The nightly backup's Supabase CLI was `latest` (security
  audit of 2026-10-16, finding I): a release that changed the dump's shape
  or broke it would have reached the backups unread. It is pinned to
  2.121.0, the version the last three nightly runs used (released 14 Oct
  2026); `tests/dbbackup.js` holds a pinned version. STANDARD.md names what
  stays the user's: versioning or Object Lock on `private/backups/`, and a
  restore rehearsal.

- 2026-10-17 · The CDN scripts carried no integrity hash (security audit
  of 2026-10-16, finding J): a CDN serving other bytes under the pinned
  version would have run them in the console and on every client page.
  Each portal page's Supabase and QR library tags now carry `integrity`
  (sha384 of the file the CDN serves, read through the proxy twice and
  checked in Chromium against those bytes) and `crossorigin="anonymous"`;
  the root pages are the user's and were not touched. Every browser suite
  answers the Supabase library with the stand-in, which no hash matches,
  so the suites' server is now `tests/serve.js` (http-server's answers,
  the attribute taken off a page as it is served) in gate.sh, snap.sh and
  by hand; `tests/sql.js` holds every tag pinned. Not covered: pdf-lib and
  fontkit, loaded on demand by `ADspaceDocs.lib()` (the PDF suites serve
  their own copies of those).

- 2026-10-17 · Mistake: the full gate on 13fc4d4 (tests c1aad16) failed
  `work` alone, a fault in the suite. It ran at midnight in Malaysia: from
  23:30 the first meeting slot is tomorrow's 00:00, nothing on that day
  comes before it, so the suite's "time already gone" (00:01) was booked
  and the sheet shut under the next field. Reproduced by holding the
  page's clock at 23:40; the suite now holds it at 15:10 for the slot
  checks (tests 066fd80). Every other suite, `ui`, uxaudit and matrix
  passed.

- 2026-10-17 · A letter takes its quotation's rates only while the
  quotation stands (the review of the audit's fix batches, finding 2).
  LETTERS PRICED AS QUOTED priced a letter at the quotation's term
  percentage and SST whenever every line carried one `quotation_id`; the
  link is never cleared and the quotation's validity was never read, so a
  renewal on the same confirmed lines (crm.js sends `renewal` down the
  same path) or a replacement after the quotation lapsed charged the SST
  of the day it was quoted. `issue_letter` (`2026-10-17-letters-priced-as-
  quoted-while-valid.sql`) and the page's `quoteOf` now take them only
  where it is not a renewal, the quotation is not removed and its
  `valid_until` is today or later in Malaysia; otherwise today's rates.
  `tests/lettersql.js` holds a valid, a last-day, an expired, a removed
  quotation and a renewal after SST moved from 6% to 8%.

  of the audit's fix batches, finding 3). Since LETTERS PRICED AS QUOTED a

  percentage on it, rounded line by line: on #530's figures the rows

- 2026-10-17 · WhatsApp messages are no longer lost as Not confirmed
  (the review of the audit's fix batches, finding 4). `wa-send` claimed
  twenty rows a round, five rounds, at up to 25 seconds a send: past the
  edge function's time, so the rows it never reached stayed at Sending
  and `wa_claim` marked them Not confirmed five minutes later, never
  sent. A DNS or connect failure, which certainly sent nothing, was also
  Not confirmed. Now the drain claims one row at a time and starts no
  send after 90 seconds (`DRAIN_BUDGET_MS`, the last send's 25 seconds
  still inside 150); `wa_claim` gives one row unless asked, five at most
  (`2026-10-17-whatsapp-queue-a-few-at-a-time.sql`); and a request whose

  connection staying Not confirmed. `tests/wafn.js` holds the claims,
  the budget and each failure; `tests/sql.js` the cap.

  letter as `quote_adjust` totals it: a line with its term ticked is

- 2026-10-17 · The client portal's meetings start on Malaysia's month (the
  review of the audit's fix batches, finding 8). MALAYSIA TIME IN THE
  DATABASE wrote `portal_meetings`' window as `date_trunc('month', now() at
  time zone 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur') at time zone 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur' - interval
  '3 months'`; `at time zone` binds before `-`, so the three months were
  taken on the UTC calendar (in March: 29 November MYT, not 1 December).
  `2026-10-17-portal-meetings-from-malaysias-month.sql` subtracts first,
  then converts. #529's migration held the shape nowhere else;
  `tests/sql.js` now fails any last definition that takes months off a
  converted moment, and evaluates the window on a UTC server.

- 2026-10-17 · The Malaysia time guard reads every day taken off a moment

- 2026-10-18 · A WhatsApp outage spends no try. The drain stopped at a
