The words moved to `health_wordings` (version 1 seeded with the words shown since 2026-10-07); `health_consent(p_on, p_wording)` refuses a version that is not the latest and `health_agreed` stands only on the latest. The old one-argument call stays for an open page and agrees to version 1 alone (no drop).

- 2026-10-18 — A check-in keeps its half month (Team audit 18). `health_checkin_save` filed answers under the half month of the moment they arrived, so a sheet opened on the 15th and saved after midnight went, unseen, into the next half. The page now names the half its sheet showed (`p_half`); an ended one is refused `stale-half` and the sheet names the half open. The two-argument call stays for an open page.

- 2026-10-18 — A half month's reminder always comes (Team audit 19). `remind_before_days` goes up to 14, and the health reminder went out that many days before a half month's end; February's second half is 13 or 14 days, so at 13 or 14 its day fell in the first half and nobody was reminded. `my_hr_remind` now holds the days to the half's own length.

- 2026-10-18 — A leaver's talks are closed (Team audit 20). Open health talks asked of a colleague were withdrawn only on a removal, so a colleague set inactive or whose access expired left talks open that nobody could hold. A trigger of its own (`team_members_talks_closed`, after an update of `active`) withdraws every open talk they asked or were asked; the leaving trigger, which holds a delete the connector cannot apply, was not restated.

- 2026-10-18 — A new colleague is added plain (Team audit 3). `team_members_system_guard` fires on update alone, so a page inserting at Team Full Access could send `system = true` (a row no page could change or remove), or a `removed_at` / `erased_at`. Trigger `team_members_insert_guard` refuses all three on a signed-in insert; the connector and the SQL Editor are not held.

- 2026-10-18 — A removal stands (Team audit 4). `team_access_guard` checked only the new row's `removed_at`, so one REST write sending `active = true, removed_at = null` brought a removed colleague back; and an expired-then-removed colleague kept `expired_at`, so moving their date reactivated them. With a sign-in a removal and an erasure are now fixed once made, and the expiry's way back passes over a removed row; the SQL Editor may still put a removal right.

- 2026-10-18 — A colleague's row is never deleted (Team audit 5). Policy `team_admin` was `for all`, so Team Full Access or an admin could hard-delete a colleague's row over REST, cascading into reviews, commissions, health and notifications with no activity entry. It is split into `team_insert` and `team_update` at Team Full Access with no delete policy. The connector held the `drop policy` (a drop), so it ran in the SQL Editor.

- 2026-10-18 — The team list holds what every colleague needs (Team audit 6). `team_read` let any active colleague read every column of every colleague over REST, the mobile hidden from the namecard, the access dates, the removal and the access map included. The table now grants a browser only the columns pages read; Team reads whole rows through `team_rows()` at Team View, and My Work asks `team_task_takers()` for who takes tasks. Released in three steps (functions, pages, grants) so no open page met a refused read before its replacement was live.

- 2026-10-18 — A sign-in email moves only through an admin (Team audit 7; the user's decision). `team_admin_guard` held the email on an admin's row alone, so Team Full Access could re-point a colleague's sign-in email and sign in as them. A trigger of its own, `team_email_guard`, refuses anybody but an admin; it is not folded into `team_admin_guard`, whose body holds the word the connector stops on.

- 2026-10-18 — An invitation goes to a colleague (Team audit 8). `invite-member` made a login for any address with only Team: Send invitation and no limit. A team invitation now needs an active colleague's address, and every invitation is claimed of the database first, twenty a caller in 24 hours (a security limit, not a business figure, so held in the function as the link lock's counts are).

- 2026-10-18 — A stale team save is refused (Team audit 9). The member sheet writes every field and a group its whole access map, so two people editing one colleague or group overwrote each other. `team_roles` gained `updated_at` (trigger `team_roles_touch`; a colleague's is stamped by `team_role_defaults`), and the pages write held to the stamp read, as a client's request is (audit C2): no row answered is told apart from a refusal by reading the stamp again.

- 2026-10-18 — Removed colleagues free their details (Team audit 10). A colleague who returns cannot be reinstated (a removal stands, so a removed row is never made active again), so they are added again; but the name, email and Employee ID indexes counted the removed row and refused the new one, and the page read every such refusal as "That email is already on the list.". Reinstate was not offered, by the earlier decision that a removal stands; the three indexes now leave out removed rows, the page names the field that clashes, and `media-pass`, `sign-download`, `sign-upload` and `invite-member`, which read a colleague by email with `.maybeSingle()`, read the active row first so two rows sharing an address never error. Every SQL lookup by email already asks an active colleague, and `hr_member_of` names nobody where two rows hold an Employee ID. The connector holds the three `drop index` lines, run in the SQL Editor; until they run the old indexes still refuse. A different person later given a removed colleague's name would read as the person in charge of any client left with the removed one (`owner` holds a name): Delete's hand-over names that work.

- 2026-10-18 — The last admin is kept (Team audit 14). `team_member_remove` and the page's Set inactive each asked whether another admin was active and then wrote, with nothing holding the answer, so two admins removing or standing down each other at once both found the other still active and both went (shown in a test with two sessions: none left). Trigger `team_members_last_admin` takes the team's admin lock (an advisory lock to the end of the transaction) on any signed-in write that takes away an active admin and refuses `last-admin` where no other active admin stands, so the second write waits for the first and reads what it committed. The audit asked for `select … for update` on the admin rows; each write already holds its own row, so two writes locking the admin rows in turn deadlock, and the advisory lock serialises them without that. `team_member_remove` and `team_keep_one_admin` are not restated (each body holds a word the connector stops on); the trigger covers every write they make.

- 2026-10-18 — A Client ID at Active (the user: "only active clients or converted leads assign an ID", and the Supplier ID's next number for clients too). Moving a client to Active with no Client ID now asks for one, the next AC number offered from `client_code_next()` (read across every client, so a colleague who sees their own clients alone is never offered a taken one); the ID and the stage go in one write, a taken ID is refused inside the question, and trigger `clients_active_code` refuses Active with none. Every live Active client already held one. The edit form no longer sends an empty Client ID it never held.

- 2026-10-18 — A value only read is no box (the user: "note down your this mistakes … this is 2nd or 3rd times same issues, last was at the reports figures sections"). `.readfield` was written for a read-only `.input`, whose own padding keeps the words inside the shade; put on a `p` or a `div` (Reports' Amount spent beside each objective, then Send email's From, Replies go to and To) it drew the shade with no padding, the words on its edge and out of line with the fields below. `.readfield:not(.input)` is now the words alone at the field's height; `tests/suppliers.js` measures no ground, the label's edge and the height. Missed both times because the sheet's screenshot was looked at for layout, not read value by value.

- 2026-10-18 — Close link, and Add existing document (the user: "how to delete the link?"; "add entry feels weird, at first i dont even understand what does it mean"). The supplier's details form had only Reset link, which makes a new link; Close link (`supplier_link_close`) ends the open one now and Create link makes another later. Documents' Add entry, which records a document issued outside the portal, reads Add existing document on Documents, the supplier's ⋯ and a colleague's Documents.

- 2026-10-19 — The page charges the sen the database does (the third audit, item 4). `rateFor` and `taxOf` in js/money.js rounded the float product, and 1,234.50 at −5% is 1,172.7749… in a float: the page charged 1,172.77 a month where `issue_letter`, rounding the exact numeric, worked 1,172.78, so a six-month letter came out six sen short and was refused as stale on every press. A ringgit card over an S$ exchange of 3.3 missed in 270 of 13,270 rate and term pairs. Both now round through `cents()` (`Math.round(|x| × 100 + 1e-7) / 100`, as js/documents.js already did); `tests/lettersql.js` prices the letter with js/money.js itself and issues it, and checks every one of those S$ pairs against Postgres's own `round`.

- 2026-10-18 — Access ends on the minute (Team audit 15). `team_expire_access()` stands a colleague down every five minutes, and until it ran `is_team()`, `allowed()`, `ops_me()` and `me()` still answered for them, so access ending at 17:00 lasted to 17:05. Each now counts a colleague only while their moment is ahead, in the query it already runs (no function of its own, so it costs nothing per policy), and `my_access_expired()` answers the gap so sign-in reads Access expired. An admin is left to the run, which never stands down the last admin with access: holding admins here would lock out the last one. `allowed('admin')` asks only whether the colleague is an admin and is unchanged.

- 2026-10-18 — Ten notices an hour (Team audit 16). `team_notice_send` wrote a bell row and a push for every colleague on each press with no limit, so a stuck key or a misused Notices part could fill every colleague's bell and phone. A sender now sends at most ten in any hour, counted under a lock held for that sender, the eleventh refused `too-many` with the moment the next may go, said on the page as Ten notices an hour at most. The next can be sent at …. Ten is a safety limit held in the function, as an invitation's count is, not a business figure.

- 2026-10-19 — A confirmed campaign keeps its SST (the third audit, item 10). The campaign list, the campaign's rail and the selection page's booked totals called `taxOf` with no day, so a campaign confirmed at 8% would read a later rate the moment SST changed. They now pass the client's last confirmation (`campaign_confirmations`, kind `client`; the selection page reads it as `get_campaign`'s `confirmed.at`), the list reading every client confirmation in one request beside the bookings. The selection page's pending bar and confirm sheet keep today's rate: that confirmation is being made now. A campaign confirmed only by the team keying it in (kind `keyed_in`) has no client confirmation and reads today's rate on both sides, as before. `tests/confirmpage.js` §5 moves SST to 10% after an 8% confirmation.

- 2026-10-18 — A caller's address is Cloudflare's (audit 2026-10-18, item 1). `request_ip()`, `media-pass` and `sign-download` took the first X-Forwarded-For entry, which the caller writes, so a guesser sent a new address on every try and the five-try lock (#618) never held them. Read on one live request (a temporary probe function, emptied and closed within the hour, dropped by the migration): PostgREST passes the caller's X-Forwarded-For entries first and Cloudflare's address last, and `cf-connecting-ip`, which Cloudflare sets and refuses from a caller (error 1000); X-Real-IP never arrives. `request_ip()` now reads `cf-connecting-ip`, else the last entry. Cloudflare stamps a function's own address on the calls it makes for a page, so `media-pass` and `sign-download` send their caller's address in `x-adspace-ip` beside a relay secret kept in `app_secrets`, which `request_ip()` (now security definer, still closed to browsers) checks before taking it.

- 2026-10-19 — A WhatsApp link button is the record's own (third audit, item 2). `wa-send` filled a template's link button with whatever the composer sent, so a stale prefill (a recipient changed after the field was filled, or a page left open) could send one creator a button to another creator's page, or a client another client's review link. `wa_compose_prepare` now answers the approval reminder's page (`link`: `review/?k=` and the client's key, `creators/?k=` and the campaign's) beside the creator's `code` it already answered, and `wa-send` fills the button from those alone, past the button's fixed base; the page's `button_value` is no longer read. The composer shows the link button as a value only read. A template with a link button sent where the record holds no page (a plain message to a client contact) is refused `wa-no-link`: the team could type one before, which is exactly what let a wrong link go out.

- 2026-10-18 — Approve asks the passcode as the feed does (audit 2026-10-18, item 13). `submit_review` and `submit_review_seen` compared the stored passcode themselves, so a guesser locked out of `get_review_feed` after five wrong tries could go on guessing through Approve, uncounted. Both now ask `link_passcode('review', …)`: a wrong one is counted with the feed's against the caller's address and still answers `not_found`; a locked caller is answered `locked` with its minutes, which the review page shows as Not sent. Found by the audit; `tests/confirmonce.js` mixes wrong tries across the feed and both decisions and locks on the fifth.

- 2026-10-19 — Typed text is never drawn as markup (the third audit, item 6). The client record's facts and the campaign's facts drew any value beginning `<span` as HTML, so the muted Not set could be built inline; Industry, Source and the push format are typed text, so a stored `<span onmouseover=…>` ran in every colleague's console. A fact not set is now `null`, drawn as Not set, and everything else is escaped. js/form.js's finder `escHtml` now escapes all five characters as every other copy does (its two uses are text, so this is hardening). The 37 `esc` copies stay apart. `tests/crm.js` and `tests/camp.js` store markup in Industry and the push format.

- 2026-10-18 — A client's device follows only a link that opens (audit 2026-10-18, item 5). `push_target`'s client branch matched the campaign's key alone, so anyone holding the key could have a device told of a campaign's drafts and posts without the passcode `get_campaign` asks for, and after its client went Past. It now finds the campaign only where it has no passcode and its client is not Past; `push_subscribe` answers `not-found` otherwise. Checking the passcode instead was not done: `push_subscribe` takes no passcode and the page that would send it (`js/creators.js`) is another session's file, and no campaign held a passcode on the day. A device that followed a campaign before it took a passcode stays until it is turned off in the browser or the push service lets it go. `tests/sql.js` holds both refusals.

- 2026-10-18 — An invoice is signed only under its campaign's own client (audit 2026-10-18, item 3). `sign-download` signed any stored `private/{uuid}/{uuid}.pdf` a campaign's `invoice_url` named, so a key written under another client's folder (a report's kept PDF, say) would have been handed to that campaign's console reader and its selection page. Both paths now read the campaign's `client_id` (the console as the colleague, the selection page with the service role by its key, after `get_campaign` has proved the link) and refuse `bad_key` unless the key begins `private/{that client id}/`. Live on the day: both private invoices sat under their own client's folder. `tests/signdownloadfn.js` runs the function as deployed and failed on the old code.

- 2026-10-18 — Bukku, phase 1: contacts (the user: "build API that push the client or supplier details over to Bukku"; approved with the rule that a company's name is in capitals and a person's each word capitalised). The portal never makes a quotation or an invoice in Bukku yet; it sends the contact by hand, so the team's Bukku keeps one contact a company. Many clients already stand in Bukku under codes the team made, so a send first offers the contacts with the same registration number, then the same or a similar name, and links one rather than making a second; a new contact takes Bukku's own next code for the name's first letter (C-L0012), as the team's codes run. The Client ID and Supplier ID ride in custom fields the team made in Bukku, chosen once on the Settings page, never typed. An update reads the contact first and sends back what Bukku holds (code, terms, accounts, groups, other people and addresses) with the portal's fields set over it, so a send never undoes what accounts set in Bukku; the types only gain. A supplier that is also a client is the same contact. The NRIC and bank details stay in the portal (the NRIC goes as the registration number of an individual only to a colleague holding Supplier bank details). Sending is by hand because a send changes another system's records; nothing is sent on a save. The token and subdomain are Supabase secrets alone. The live Bukku was never written to while it was built: `bukkufn` runs the function's own code against a stand-in.

- 2026-10-18 — Passcode tries are kept for a time (audit 2026-10-18, item 14). `link_tries` keeps each caller's address for every link they typed a passcode on, and nothing removed a row, so the addresses stayed for good. `privacy_retention` (the 2nd of each month) now removes a row whose last try and last opening are over 30 days old and whose lock has ended. An address that opened the link within 30 days is kept, since the link's own lock spares it. The function holds `delete`, so the connector holds it: it is run in the SQL Editor, and it stands in for HEALTH DATA KEPT FOR A TIME's restatement, which had not been run yet. `tests/sql.js` keeps an opened, a locked and a recent address and removes two quiet ones.

- 2026-10-19 — A WhatsApp message sent by hand is filed before it goes (third audit, item 9). `wa-send` asked Sent recently, sent, and filed the message only once Meta answered, so two presses close together (two tabs, a press while the answer was slow) both passed the check and both sent. `wa_send_begin` now takes a lock on the recipient, the purpose and the record, refuses `sending` while the same message is on its way and `recent` unless Send again was answered, and files the row as Sending, all before Meta is asked; `wa_send_done` closes the sender's own row. Shown with two sessions: the second waited for the first and was refused. A send Meta never confirmed was filed Failed by `wa_sent`, so it did not count as sent and could go again unasked; it is now Not confirmed, as the queue's are. The sends from before the composer (`report`, `feedback` and `wa_creator_send`) skipped the check altogether; no page has called them since the composer (2026-10-10), so they are closed (a revoke, not a drop, which the connector holds). `wa_sent` stays callable for one release, for the wa-send deployed before this.

- 2026-10-18 — What a client types is held to a length (audit 2026-10-18, item 12). The functions a page with no sign-in writes through (`submit_review`, `review_draft`, `confirm_selection`, `confirm_selection_with`, `creator_submit`, `portal_request_once`) took a name, a note or a caption of any length, so one call could write megabytes into the reviews, the requests and the Activity record. Each now refuses past 80 characters for a name, 2,000 for a note and 5,000 for a caption, after the link is proved and before anything is written; `submit_review_seen` and `portal_request` call them and refuse alike. The pages were left without `maxlength`: no real input comes near the limits (Instagram's own caption limit is 2,200), and a refusal reads as Not sent. `tests/confirmonce.js` holds each refusal and each limit taken.

- 2026-10-18 — A miss: #659 (Approve asks the passcode) shipped with `tests/seensql.js` red. That suite builds the schema's last `submit_review` on a cut-down fixture with no `link_passcode`, and the release ran `confirmonce` and `sql` but not every Postgres suite that cuts the function. Found running the suites for item 12; the fixture now stands in for the two helpers. The rule stands as written: a changed function runs every suite that calls it (`grep -l`), Postgres suites included.

- 2026-10-19 — Last activity in one read (the third audit, item 7). The Clients list read every call and visit, every Letter of Offer and every document to find each client's newest, three reads with no paging, so past PostgREST's thousand rows a table the newest facts were dropped and a client read as quiet that was not. `client_last_activity()` answers the newest of each kind per client (a removed call and a date ahead of now left out), as the caller, so each table's read policy and the client scope decide what a colleague is answered as before. Applied before the page; an open page from before still reads the three tables. `tests/sql.js` answers 1,500 clients past a thousand rows.

- 2026-10-19 — Content Review's counts from the database (the third audit, item 8). The client list paged through every post and every decision of every set to count change requests, and a client's set list read its posts unpaged (cut at a thousand) and then all their decisions. Both now ask `review_set_counts(p_sets)` once, as My Work and the Dashboard already did: the posts and the change requests of each set, by the decision standing on the round on show. The stand-in's copy no longer caps at 500 sets, as the database stopped doing on 2026-10-18. `tests/sets.js` counts the requests.

- 2026-10-19 — The wake calls carry a secret, once a transaction (third audit, item 17). `wa-send`'s `drain` and `push-send` run with Verify JWT off, since pg_net calls with no session, and asked nothing of the caller, so anybody could make them work through the queues on demand; and every queued row woke its sender again, so a notice to forty colleagues started forty runs of `push-send`. A wake secret is now made once in `app_secrets` (from `gen_random_uuid`, a strong source, so the file needs no extension schema); `wa_kick` and `push_kick` send it as `x-adspace-wake` and each function asks `wake_secret_ok`, the service role's alone, before reading a key or claiming a row. The audit asked for the secret as an edge function secret as well as in the database: a dashboard secret is entered by hand and would have to be copied out of the database through a person, so the functions read it from the database through the service role, as `push-send` already reads its VAPID keys; the value is never shown. The wakes are once a transaction (a local setting), not once a statement: pg_net sends after the commit, so one wake finds every row the transaction queued.

- 2026-10-19 — A meeting is booked once (third audit, item 16). meet-create posted a new Google Calendar event whenever the record held none, so two presses close together (or a press after a save that never arrived) booked two events, and the second save left the first on the shared calendar with nobody holding it. The event now takes an id made from the record's (`admonth` or `adtouch` and the record id's hex, inside Google's 0-9 and a-v), so Google answers the second 409 and the function returns the event the first made. Two things the fixed id needed: the slot check would have named the record's own event as the clash, so it is left out like a stored event; and Google keeps a deleted event's id, so Delete then Create Google Meet would meet 409 on a cancelled event, which is now put back, confirmed, with a new Meet. Events made before keep their random ids and are moved as before. `tests/meetfn.js` books two events against the file before the fix.

- 2026-10-19 — The Dashboard's work figures in one request (the third audit, item 19). The Dashboard asked `ops_report` eight times a visit (the period, the one before it, each of six months). `ops_reports(p_ranges)` calls `ops_report` itself for each span, as the caller, and answers them in order, so every figure is ops_report's own; the page asks it once a visit and once a period, the six months only the first time. The audit also asked to bound the read of every set ever made behind "No set this month" to this month; that read also gives "Last set {day}", which this month alone would blank, so it reads the last twelve months instead. `tests/ops.js` holds the answers equal to ops_report's; `tests/overview.js` counts one request.

- 2026-10-19 — The Activity record by subject (the third audit, item 11). A client's and a campaign's Activity read `activity_log` by subject, newest first, and the table, kept three years, was indexed on its time alone. `activity_log_subject_idx` on (subject, created_at desc) answers that read; applied live. `tests/sql.js` reads the plan.

- 2026-10-19 — Eleven retired functions dropped (the third audit, item 15): `wa_recent`, `wa_template_save`, `team_set_expiry`, `namecard_save_mine`, `namecard_save_card`, `perf_guard_set`, `video_script_create`, `report_partner_save`, `report_partner_set_active`, `sm_report_white_label`, `sm_report_label`. Each was kept for a page loaded before its successor and each was still callable by any signed-in browser; nothing in the portal, its edge functions, workers, policies, triggers or other functions names one (read live). Their tests were removed or moved onto direct SQL where a later check needed the state they made; the stand-in refuses them as PostgREST will. `tests/sql.js` fails a page, edge function or worker that names one again. The drop is run in the SQL Editor (the connector holds a `drop`).

- 2026-10-19 — A moved date's notice reads as the house writes it (the third audit, item 20). `ops_log` wrote a task's moved first draft or final date with `to_char(…, 'DD Mon YYYY')`: "05 Sep 2026" in the bell and the push, where the portal writes "5 Sept 2026", and on the database's UTC clock, so a date at midnight in Malaysia read as the day before. It now names the Malaysian day through `register_day`; every other line of ONE PRESS, ONE NOTICE is unchanged. Other `to_char` dates in older activity lines were left as they are: they are history, not this item. `tests/ops.js` checks the notice.

- 2026-10-19 — On time counts the work still late (the user, with a screenshot: "there are late tasks yet showing 100% on time delivery"). `ops_report`'s `on_time` counted only the tasks that reached client review in the period, so a task past its deadline and still short of its review sat in neither figure: the ring read 100% beside three late tasks. `on_time` now also answers `late_open`, the open tasks late by the report's own late rule, counted in the period their first missed deadline fell in and in any period that runs to now (its end within ten minutes of now, since the page names the moment it asks a little before the database reads it; the first build read `p_to >= now()` and counted none, which `tests/overview.js` caught). The ring and On-time delivery by month read met over reached plus late_open; the month table's column reads Due. `tests/ops.js` places a late task in its period, in the period running to now and in no closed period after; `tests/overview.js` holds the ring's Late part at least every late task.

- 2026-10-19 — Documents moved beside the services they quote (the user: "the documents under client section is troublesome. It shows quotations and services lines but when creating documents it has to go into below Account to create. Troublesome n extra steps"). A client record's Documents part sat in the Account tab, under Contacts and Billing, while the quotations and service lines a Letter of Offer is issued from sat in Services. The Services tab now holds Quotations, Service lines and Documents, one under the other; Account holds Contacts and Billing. Each part keeps its own address, so `tab=documents` (the Overview's Letters, the rail's next step) opens Services on Documents. Only the grouping moved: the parts, their permissions and the letter sheet are unchanged.

- 2026-10-19 — My Work's Completed on Last month ends where this month begins (logged by the full gate of 2026-10-18). Finished work is read from the earlier of the period's start and the week's (the week always, for Completed today), and the Completed and All lists showed every finished row the read brought: on Last month, work finished this month too, and on any period the week overhung, the days before it. `inFilter` now keeps a finished task only inside the chosen period (`inPeriod`, `periodEnd()` for Last month); open work and the search are unchanged. `tests/work.js` holds work finished today out of Last month and back in This month.

- 2026-10-19 — Posted on time on the Dashboard (the user asked what on-time delivery compares; it compares the day a task first reaches client review with its Due date. Asked whether Scheduled against the post date would be truer, the advice was that the time between review and Scheduled is the client's approval, so it would count the client's delay against the team, and that the true client-facing promise is going live by the post date, kept as its own figure; the user: "Build posted on time on the dashboard. Keep ontime this way"). `ops_report` also answers `posted` (due, met): content whose post date fell in the period (MYT) and has passed, or which went live, met where it went live on or before its post date's day; a workflow with a live stage, never cancelled or archived, within the reader's client scope; a post due today and not yet live waits for tomorrow. It reads as `perf_ops_rate`'s On-time posting does for one colleague. The glance draws a second ring beside On-time delivery, and On time by month carries both lines with both figures in its table. `tests/ops.js` and `tests/overview.js` hold it.

- 2026-10-19 — Bukku as Bukku holds it (the user, with a screenshot of Send to Bukku: "the bukku address follow Address line 1, address line 2, postal code, city, state, country. But portal fields only one big field … also can allow link or sync without changing info"; "your salutation didnt follow over even though contact alr added salutation"; then "shouldnt tick default shipping. Just default billing would do, payment term"). `bukku-sync` put the whole typed address in Bukku's street, so every linked client read as a change (Bukku held the street, postcode, city and state apart) and a line break followed by a comma read ",,". - 2026-10-20 — An approved supplier's details form stood open, and an update meant typing everything again (the user, on BRIQ PACKAGING's record: Active since 18 Oct, its details form "Sent, open until 2 Nov"; then "if one supplier that has been registered and approved … would like to change record, how could this be done from supplier side?", and "why did the gate didnt catch the open link"). What broke: the link was made after the supplier was approved, and nothing ended it, so the supplier could send new details, its bank account included, with nobody asking (the answers still waited on Use details, so nothing was written by itself). Why: the rules said what a link does while a supplier is Pending, and never what becomes of it once the supplier moves on; Close link (2026-10-18) was added for this case by hand and no rule tied it to approval. How it was found: the user's screenshot; the full gate on 6f9d206 passed, because no suite approved a supplier with a link open and no rule said it should close. The fix: a move of status ends every open link; an Active supplier is sent an update link that opens on the details held but never the NRIC or the bank details (left blank, they are kept; the link opens with no sign-in, so it shows nothing a payment hangs on), the record reads each change from and to, and a new payee, bank or account sends the supplier back to Pending to be approved again, against a payment redirected by a changed account. The page also put the state and the ⋯ on the name's line on a phone (they had wrapped under it), moved an open update link under Payment details, said an unlinked client in one line, and stopped naming the system account as the approver. The general rule in CLAUDE.md: a link handed out for one step ends when its record moves past that step, and a suite seeds it open at that move. Checked against it: the client details form never writes the record and its billing may be asked again after Active by design; a campaign's selection link stays for the results by design; a website quotation's link is refused for every act once it expires.

- 2026-10-21 — The seven logged `sql` and `smsql` failures were the test database's clock, never the functions (the user: "Diagnose those"). What broke: two `sql` checks (`review_set_counts`' oldest change, `client_last_activity`'s days since a letter) and five `smsql` report deadline checks failed on 2026-10-20 on main and the wave 2 branch alike, and passed again the next morning. Why: each Postgres suite runs `initdb`, which takes its time zone from the shell, and the run had been started on Malaysia time; the live database runs on UTC. A fixture's date literal (`'2026-10-03'`) then meant 2 Oct 16:00 UTC, and a check comparing `current_date` (MYT) with a UTC day was a day out between midnight and 8am MYT. How it was found: both suites passed at 08:40 MYT with the shell on UTC, and run again with `TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur` they failed exactly the logged seven (one `sql` check at any hour, the other only before 8am). The fix: every one of the thirteen Postgres suites starts its cluster with `-c timezone=UTC` (tests d2ad3eb), and both pass under a Malaysian shell. The gate's own lane already kept the machine's clock, so it never showed them; a suite run by hand did. The logged defects are removed.

### 2026-10-22 — Read from Bukku asks which codes; a tax code can be deleted
- The user, 2026-10-22: "Read from bukku for sst codes pull in 32 items for
  taxes which i only uses 0% no tax or 8% SST. And you didnt provide option
  to delete this is a mistake or error", then "When importing let to choose
  before direct import n provide all delete options mentioned many times".

  team uses NT and SV8), and the table was built so a code could only be
  stood down, never deleted. Both went against what the user had asked
  before: choose before importing, and a way to delete what is added.
- Now Read from Bukku lists Bukku's codes with ticks (those offered already
  ticked) and keeps only the ticked ones; each code's ⋯ holds Delete and
  Select deletes several (the count typed back). A code a service line, a
  quotation or a letter names is refused by name and stays (it can be set
  not offered), so an issued letter keeps the code it names.
- The rule is written as a standing one in CLAUDE.md (Writes, refusals,
  reversibility): an import lists what it found and takes what is ticked;
  whatever can be added can be deleted.

  report, an S$ quotation or an S$ letter; the rest read RM.

  picks the currency alone.

  foot named `ctx`, out of scope in the preview's answer (`B.ctx`), so the
  lines drew the error in place of the quotation; and the one-time S$ seed
  read `sm_reports` directly, which a cut-down database lacks (now each

### 2026-10-22 — A PDF in the installed app has a way out
- Reported by the user: "when pdf generated from PWA there is no button to
  share to close the windows whatsoever".
- Cause: every Preview, and every save on an iPhone or iPad, opened a
  window at the press (`ADspaceDocs.tabFor()` and four copies of `openTab()`
  in reports, scripts, checklists and register) and pointed it at the
  worker's `/admin/file/…` (or `/client/file/…`) or a blob:. In the
  installed app that address is inside the app's own scope, so the PDF
  opened inside the standalone app with no browser bar: no Share, no Done,
  no Back, the person stuck until the app was closed. In Safari the same
  flow worked, its own bar giving the way out.
- Fix: `ADspaceDocs.installed()` (display-mode standalone or
  `navigator.standalone`, on iOS or an Android touch screen) is the one
  test. There `tabFor()` and `previewTab()` (the one Preview opener, which
  replaced the four copies) open nothing; `save()` hands the share sheet the
  named File (the PDF with its name, Save to Files, Print, WhatsApp, a
  close), asking File ready · Share (分享) when the press has gone stale; and
  where the app has no share sheet for files the PDF is shown in a sheet
  (`#pdfViewSheet`) with Close and Download. The windows opened for a
  signed Handbook file and a campaign invoice go to another origin, which
  the installed app opens in Safari's own viewer with Done; left alone.
- Proof: `tests/pwapdf.js` (new) on an iPhone and Android in the installed
  app: no window opened, the named File shared, File ready · Share after a
  stale press, the viewer with Close, Escape and Download where share is
  missing, a browser tab still opening its tab at the press, and a scan of
  every script for a blank window opened outside ADspaceDocs. Only an
  iPhone can confirm the share sheet itself: the user checks it on the
  installed app.

### 2026-10-22 · `revise` fed a picture to a video
`tests/revise.js` "and one without asks for its first frame, inline" failed
on main once REV-5 (#712) put a shaded `.thumb-miss` tile in place of a
thumbnail whose file fails. The page was right: the suite answered every
`mycdn.adspace.me` address with a PNG, so the reel's `.mov` did not decode,
fired `error`, and REV-5 replaced the `<video>` the check looks for. The
suite now answers a video address (`.mov`, `.mp4`, `.webm`) with a 16px
WebM the browser plays, keeps the PNG for pictures and a 404 for a `gone.`
file, and seeds Picture gone to assert the missing tile, never a broken
image. The assertion is unchanged. Rule: a suite that answers the CDN
answers a video with a video (CLAUDE.md §1, harness facts).

### 2026-10-27 · The quotation website reads the portal's type
- Reported by the user from an iPhone: /quote/'s buttons, words and title
  did not match the rest of the portal, and the proportions were off.
- Cause: `.shell.qs` set `--ctl-text` and `--field-text` to 16px, so every
  button and field read 16 against the portal's 13 and 14; the title stood
  at 21 on a phone over a 16px lead, no step of φ; the lead sat apart from
  its title. `tests/quotesite.js` asserted the 16, so the gate held the
  fault in place, and uxaudit's `ctlh` read the height tokens alone: the
  controls were equal to each other, which is all `row-height` measures.
- Fix: the page takes the tokens (a control's words 13, 14 under a finger;
  a field's 14, 15), its count stepper the small control; the title 26px
  (16 × φ) at every width with the lead 8px under it. `ctlh` now also fails
  a page setting `--ctl-text` or `--field-text` to its own figure, and the
  suite asserts the tokens.
